Lietuvoszinios", 2014 01 141 Lietuvosbankas Interview of Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Lithuanian Bank's Management, to the daily newspaper "Lietuvoszinios", 14/01/2014 2014-01-14 Vita Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Lithuanian Bank's Management, is interviewed by Ruta Grigolyt - Does the deliberations about whether you're going to adopt the euro, the "ushers'" talk of a referendum, make sense yet? - There's no need to laugh at lithuania. nor the whole world in such deliberations . The introduction of the euro is not a one-day job, it does not happen with a click of a finger. This is a process that requires long preparation. Business, government authorities, the central bank are preparing for it, systems are being reorganized. As these processes gain momentum, we begin to consider whether the euro should be adopted. funny and pointless. Finally, joining the euro area is an inevitable process. The Treaty of Accession to the European Union (EU) contains m, from, it is made clear that, from the moment of accession to the Community, Lithuania joins the Economic Monetary Union with a reservation concerning the euro. This derogation shall disappear when the State fulfils the convergence criteria. In 2014, there will be a mass periodic, biennial assessment of Lithuania's compliance with those criteria and, if so, of the process is automatic. And the referendum has already taken place more than 1Omets ago. Everything else is a political derivation- giggles and nothing more. - There is no silence among the Labour Party's representatives about the further increase in the minimum monthly wage. Will this be a threat to the introduction of the euro and what kind? - It is not correct to associate the euro issue with a mine-sensitive salary. It's about ingi things. The increase or non-increase in the minimum wage is judged by very objective economic parameters. It is customary to believe that the ratio of the minimum wage to the average wage should be one to two . So there's no talk of that yet. An increase in the minimum wage in a short period of time immediately affects the labor market, competitiveness, and 1/4 03/08/22, 14:58 Lietuvosbanko valdybospirmininkoVito Vasiliauskointerviudienrasiui "Lietuvoszinios",2014 01 14 J Lietuvosbankas at the same time - and for the rest of economic life. So there can be no quick, unmeasured solutions in this regard. Has be very clear calculations, and so far I do not see any prerequisites for raising the minimum wage, since it has already been increased- dinta. Let's evaluate the economic parameters, and then let's talk about it. - Politicians who want to argue can resort to the argument that the 2013 indicators will be evaluated, so in 2014 something can be changed and "slipped through". - That would be the biggest mistake to think about it, because no one in the world and in Europe needs that assessment of our indicators, just ourselves. The euro is not a panacea or an end goal, it is the key to the desired future, a condition for creating a certain well-being. In Lithuania, we have all the instruments to maintain financial discipline so that the economy, to put it simply, does not smoke through the chimney. We have also learned our lesson during the crisis, so there is a law on fiscal discipline, based on the mechanisms of the EU, where it is made clear that a country's economic development, fiscal and budgetary policies must be sustainable. So whether there is a euro or not, we will certainly not be able to spend. - Is it possible to change taxes for a year remaining before the introduction of the euro, to introduce new ones? - It's a matter for a sovereign country. Everything can be done, but you need to measure very well, calculate forecasts, what the consequences will be. It is clear that, when it comes to meeting the criteria, the focus must be on the budget deficit and sustainability in the future. If taxes were to be raised, for example, on consumption, this would, of course, affect the prices of goods and services, and it would have to be calculated how this would affect inflation. You cannot make sudden changes without first finding out what we are aiming for with those changes. However, sometimes in our state such a calculation is lacking, although there are many experts in Lithuania who are able to do it. I think we need to forget about political ambitions and sit quietly at the calculations. - Experience, however, shows that experts are calculating, and the Government is scrambling to these calculations by hand and doing it in their own way. - I would not like to talk about the political aspects, but there is a Government programme. It clearly sets out the objectives, objectives, distinguishes priorities separately and moves towards their implementation. In what way they are achieved - only questions of form. - When it comes to ensuring that, with the introduction of the euro, businessmen are abused by raising prices, there is perhaps a mere mention of honour agreements,,,abering's publicity and so on. Will there be no economic sanctions? 2/4 03/08/22, 14:58 Lietuvosbanko valdybospirmininkoVito Vasiliauskointerviudienrasiui "Lietuvoszinios",2014 01 14 J Lietuvosbankas - We have the law on the introduction of the euro, the plan of measures for the implementation of the national plan for the introduction of the euro, where very much clearly listed measures aimed at containing the recalculation of prices. The first envisaged mechanism is mas is an advertisement for prices in both currencies. It will be required that prices be changed at a fixed rate, without any increase. These prices will have to be published at points of sale for several months before the introduction of the euro, and half a year after introduction. On the other hand, there are administrative controls for which the Member States are empowered to carry out tybic Consumer Rights Protection Service, the State Inspectorate of Non-Food Products and the State Food and Veterinary Service. These authorities will control that there are no errors or abuses in the recalculation of prices. Statistics Lithuania will also publish prices in certain periods, it will be possible to compare them. However, sanctions are also provided for the use of the currency exchange at the time of price conversion. Those sanctions are certainly considerable: they are liability both under the prohibition of unfair commercial practices for consumers and under the Code of Administrative Offences. It is also aimed at signing memoranda with business structures, through publicity campaigns, aspects of the prestige of companies, to seek to avoid taking advantage of the situation. In addition, all sellers of goods and services operate in a competitive environment, and agreements on changing prices are hardly possible. The practice of the countries that have adopted the euro shows very clearly that the impact on prices is present, but on average it is 0.2-0.3%, so from 100 litas it would be about 20-30 cents. About a quarter of the goods in the consumer's basket are affected. It should be emphasized that prices or inflation depend on the general cycle of the economy. If Lithuania is converging with the EU, it is approaching the Community averages in all economic respects: according to the average income, the standard of living, prices cannot fall out of context. By the way, if you look at the statistics of the countries that have recently introduced the euro, in four out of five, wages have risen faster than prices. - How will the income of the population be recalculated - salaries,social benefits? - The law strictly states that it must be recalculated at a fixed rate, there can be no rounding. However, if they are necessary in some way, they must be done for the benefit of consumers. With regard to the recalculation of salaries or contributions, it is said that if the sixth decimal place is 0.1, then it is rounded to 1, and therefore to the positive side. This is done so that the euro is not the cause of the slightest decline in income. - What awaits people who have taken out loans in litas? How will the interest rate change for them, how much will the loan become cheaper or more expensive? Will banks have the right to charge them fees for changing the terms of the contract? 3/4 03/08/22, 14:58 Lietuvosbanko valdybospirmininkoVito Vasiliauskointerviudienrasiui "Lietuvoszinios",2014 01 14 J Lietuvosbankas The user will not have to do anything, everything will go automatically. VILIBOR (lending interest in litas - ed.) will change to EURIBOR (lending interest in euros - ed.), and our calculations show that in the long term this will help residents save. Euribor is currently lower than VILIBOR, and usually always that's how it was. There really can't be a one-sided requirement to rewrite contracts unless both parties agree on it. Incidentally about 70 prae. all loans issued in Lithuania are in euro. - How long will it take for the situation to stabilise, when will we be able to realistically assess whether we are experiencing benefits or vice versa? - Technical currency exchange, of course, will be a one-time action, and from January 1, euros will be the only means of payment. However, under the current bill, litas as a means of payment at points of sale will still be accepted for the first two weeks. At post offices, it will be possible to change them for free in the first two months, in commercial banks - in the first half of the year, and in certain places - in the second half of the year. Subsequently, it will be possible to exchange litas at the Central Bank indefinitely. As for the impact on the economy, it is not one-time. According to our calculations, the positive impact of the euro on the Lithuanian economy in seven years - in 2015-2022 - will increase gross domestic product by an additional approximately 1.8 percent annually. That's certainly quite a few. Of course, there will be one-time expenses, which we can call a minus, but in the longer term, the entire Lithuanian economy and each of us will benefit. - We recovered the litas not so long ago,much of it - after the flag, coat of arms and anthem - is a symbol of the country's independence. How will we come to terms with this moral loss? - This is understandable, especially given that only just over 20 years have passed since independence. Sentiments towards the litas, as well as how strong the currency of interwar Lithuania are, are well understood. This sentiment will be preserved - on the reverse of the euro coins as a national symbol will be Vytis. And this is a great opportunity to promote Lithuania, because the euros with the Vytis will spread throughout Europe and the world. 4/4

Title: Speech at the European Parliaments Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (ECON) meeting
text: 03/08/22, 14:43 Vilas Vasiliauskas. Speech at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (ECON) meeting I Bank of Lith... ffl'I:) LI.ET UVQS B,AN KAS VitasVasiliauskasS. peechat the European Parliament'sEconomicand MonetaryAffairs Committee(ECON)meeting 2014-03-20 Economicand MonetaryAffairs Committee{ECON) EuropeanParliament 17 March 2014, Brussels Honourable Members, The European Parliament is a key stakeholder in the euro area enlargement process. I greatly appreciate the opportunity to provide the Committee with a fresh update on the state of the Lithuanian economy and financial sector. I believe that today 's discussion will contribute to the forming of an institutional view. I will focus on issues that are closely related to the mandate of the central bank: Q1 of 1 - Firstly, how did the Lithuanian economy react to the crisis? - Secondly, how do we see price stability? - Thirdly, what does the financial sector look like? The Lithuanian economy staged a quick recovery after the crisis and demonstrates solid growth rates. The pre-crisis level of output will be exceeded this year. The cumulative GDP increase since 2009 has been 15.3 per cent. The essential elements of the adjustment strategy have been frontloaded policy response, preserved financial stability, and economic flexibility . ... 1/3 03/08/22, 14:43 VitasVasiliauskas.Speechat the EuropeanParliament'sEconomicand MonetaryAffairsCommittee(ECON) meetingI Bankof Lith... Economic rebalancing has occurred, supported by labour and product market flexibility. The current account is close to balance. Competitiveness has improved after substantial adjustment in unit labour costs. Economic recovery was led by the tradable sector. Domestic demand has strengthened as well. Real exports are 40 per cent higher than during the pre-crisis peak. Unemployment has almost halved since the crisis peak and currently is at around the euro area average. The adjustment process confirmed that the economic structure in Lithuania is sufficiently flexible to operate under the fixed exchange rate regime. It has also confirmed the ability to adjust policies when needed. Inflationsustainability Domestic price pressures are firmly contained and inflation is comfortably below the price-stability criterion. The average annual inflation is projected to stay at 0.7 per cent in the first quarter of 2014. As regards the medium-term sustainability, the outlook is more encouraging than in the past. The effective prevention of unsustainable developments in asset prices will be ensured by macro-prudential tools. The pass-through of global price shocks in Lithuania is relatively higher due to a higher share of food and commodities prices in the consumer basket. However, with the on-going income convergence, it has been steadily declining. There are also important policy initiatives underway that will reduce energy intensity while increasing diversification of energy sources at the same time. These initiatives, notably the housing renovation program, LNG terminal, integration with the European power grid, unbundling of gas supply and distribution networks, are supported by the EU. Financialsector While there are no specific convergence criteria to detect fragilities in the financial sector, the crisis has reminded us of the important interlinkages between the financial sector and the real economy. When assessing economic sustainability and convergence, we have a strong story to tell on financial sector issues. The Lithuanian financial sector is dominated by traditional retail banking. The banking sector is not oversized and banks account for 65 per cent of GDP.The funding structure is domestically oriented. Banks fund themselves mostly through deposits, with the loan-to-depositratio at 107 per cent. The share of nonresidentdepositsis negligible- onlyabout3 per cent - and geographically diversified. . 03/08/22, 14:43 VitasVasiliauskas.Speechat the EuropeanParliament'sEconomicand MonetaryAffairsCommittee(ECON) meetingI Bankof Lith... The banking sector is well capitalized and liquid, with addressed fragilities. The banking sector has more than twice as much capital as is required by the Bank of Lithuania and nearly all of it is of the highest quality (Tier 1). The non-performing loans have been steadily declining and currently stand at 10.7 per cent. The lending conditions have normalised and there is no growth constraining debt overhang. Private sector indebtedness in Lithuania is second lowest in the EU (43.1% of nominal GDP).The loan portfolio is expected to increase by about 3 per cent in 2014. The surveys of the Bank of Lithuania also do not indicate crediting constraints on the supply side. A comprehensive macro-prudential toolkit is in place to prevent unsustainable lending practices and the macro-prudential powers of the Bank of Lithuania will be further enhanced by granting an explicit macroprudential mandate. There are binding loan-to-value, debt-to-income, and loan amortization requirements for banks. The Bank of Lithuania, as the supervisory authority, will be prepared to join the Single Supervisory Mechanism from the date of entry into the euro area. As has been noted, the financial sector is in good shape, with addressed residual risks and no legacy assets. I will stop here and will be pleased to answer your questions.

Verslozinios",2014 04 30 l Lietuvosbankas Interview of Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Lithuanian Bank Administration, to the daily newspaper "Verslozinios", 30/04/2014 2014-05-12 Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Lithuanian Bank's Management, is interviewed by DaliusSimnas. Interviewpublished on 30 April 2014 in the supplement "Banks r draudimas" of the daily newspaper "Verslozinios" - A period of significant change in the banking sector. This is related to Lithuania's planned integration into the euro area already in 2015, as well as the entrenchment of the rules of the banking union. How will the banks' operations be fully affected? If we talk about the components of banking regulation, I would single out the affairs of the banking union. General the surveillance mechanismin theeuro area enters into force since 4 November 2014 Therefore, if the decision on Lithuania's accession to the euro area is positive, m, from, Lithuania will automatically become part of the general banking supervisory mechanism from 1 January next year. Halibut means that the European Central Bank(ECB) will also be involved in our banking supervision system. First of all, it's touches our three largest banks, SEB. Swedbank and DNB,which account for 70% of the entire banking sector. Preparatory work is necessary to predict possible access - property valuation and stress tests. Halibut represents an additional adm i nistracical burden primarily on these banks. - Does this not mean that the additional costs will be directly transferred to the shoulders of customers? A good question.There will be no doubt that there will be additional costs associated with the administrative burden. First of all, and with regard to the introduction of the said property. Before the CEECB takes over banking supervision, they are assessed by auditors or other independent evaluators. Of course, it comes at a cost, but I would not think that this will simply have an impact on the increase in prices for services in the banking sector. All the more so because, although we are talking about three banks that occupy 70% of the market, there are other banks that operate in that environment and which will not have costs. As for the general environment, we do not expect anything to change radically. We live in a low-interest environment, both in terms of loans and banking flnansification. We predict that a similar environment should continue in 2014, or perhaps in terms of 1/8 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVito Vasiliauskointerviudienrasiui "Verslozinios",2014 04 30 l Lietuvosbankas further. At least the indicators for the euro area, but also for the EU as a whole, show that the low interest rate environment should be maintained. Loans the volume of the portfolio and the ratio of newly issued and repayable old loans also do not change significantly. Truth Data for the first quarter of this year show that government borrowing is shrinking, while the private sector is already more loans are issued than the old ones have returned. The growth of new loans for the private sector has been observed since 2013 m., this is how it remains this year. - How will the activities of the supervision services of the Lithuanian Bank (Bank of Lithuania) and other branches change, the number of employees when Lithuania is likely to join the banking union, as well as the fact that the country will not have its own currency after 2015 and the three largest banks will be supervised by the ECB? As you already know, LB has gone through a sufficiently significant stage of transformation. When the Bank of Lithuania was tasked with supervising the insurance and securities markets and dealing with consumer disputes with institutions providing financial services, our functions increased, but the number of employees in the bank decreased from 800 to about 600. As far as the future is concerned, it must be borne in mind that, after a possible accession to the euro area, we will have three spheres of activity that will require consideration of functions and, as a result, certain structural changes in the bank are possible. First of all, it is due to the entrenchment of the aforementioned single mechanism for banking supervision. Again, there is still a lack of clarity on how cooperation between the Bank of Lithuania and the ECB will take place. But, bearing in mind that in Lithuania 90% of our banking sector belongs to countries that will be outside the banking union, that current model of Nordic-Baltic cooperation will have to change. What it will look like, I could not say for sure at the moment, but I would certainly not think that, thanks to the transfer of the three largest banks to the ECB, we could reduce the number of staff in our supervisory authority, since the supervisory tasks and processes are indeed becoming increasingly complex Advanced. We should also talk about monetary policy, which is a relatively new thing for the Bank of Lithuania. After joining the euro area, the Bank of Lithuania will participate in the monetary policy of the ECB, i.e. our representatives will participate in the committees conducting monetary policy, and I, of course, as the head of the Central Bank of Lithuania, in the event of a positive decision on the euro, will participate in the activities of the Governing Council of the ECB. This means that we would become one of the monetary policymakers, along with the other 18 Member States of the euro area, and we would need to reform the economic and financial stability service accordingly. Until now, we have conducted monetary policy at a more theoretical level, and in reality we did not have such a real function, i.e. we still have a currency board and a fixed exchange rate of the litas. The third point I would point out is the so-called macroprudential mandate. By means of amendments to the Law on the Bank of Lithuania, which are currently being discussed in the Seimas, we ask for a mandate to systematically supervise and shape the entire financial market policy in response to possible market bubbles, to crises and using various means for this purpose. This is the implementation of the european systemic risk board function model in Lithuania. https:/ 2/8 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVito Vasiliauskointerviudienrasiui "Verslozinios",2014 04 30 l Lietuvosbankas Thus, we have three main directions, the implementation of which will affect the structural changes of the LB and, in addition to no doubt the number of employees. I believe that in the future the number of employees in our main services should definitely grow, but we also have support features that ensure that LB works as an organization. Here I see a very clear vision - more services to buy externally and thus have the optimal one in the bank the number of working people. - Will the accession to the euro area significantly reduce the cost of international transfers? When willthey align with the locals? Why are they more expensive at the moment? Indeed, today the price differences between transfers in national currency and transfers in euro are huge. On the other hand, euro transfers account for a small proportion of all transfers. It is estimated that if euro transfers become cheaper to local levels, customers of banks could save approximately 80 minutes each year. It is not worth even speculating here - you just need to pay attention to the facts of what has happened in neighboring Latvia and Estonia, which are already members of the euro area. There, the transfer rates in euro were on a par with the cost of local orders. I really don't see why anything else could happen in Lithuania. It would be very strange if we did not have a similar situation to what happened first in Estonia and then in Latvia. - What's the point of gold,foreign exchange reserves,Lithuania's transition from the euro to the euro? The generalized answer to the speculations that have been heard in the public sphere would be that nothing will change. Just as in the case of a litas, the task of foreign reserves is to cover the litas, so in the presence of the euro, the main purpose will be to cover the amount of euros put into circulation in our country. The financial assets managed by the Bank of Lithuania, foreign reserves and are the majority of Lithuania's financial assets, are not going away. When we join the euro area, we will take two steps together. Firstly, the Bank of Lithuania will fully pay its share in the capital of the European Central Bank. This is approximately EUR 43 million, and secondly, we will hand over part of the foreign reserve assets to the ECB for joint management. We will not give away, we will not give, but we will do it in the form of an exchange of property. That transfer will account for about 4-5% of the total foreign reserve assets that we will manage together with the other central bank of the euro area. Both the contribution and participation in the ECB's capital and the management of the ECB's overall foreign reserve assets will generate a return. As at present, the Bank of Lithuania will manage the remaining part of its financial assets independently. The Bank of Lithuania is owned by the state, so to say that some green people here own, I stress, 5 billion people are in power. not EUR 15 billion. EUR,as we sometimes hear, and does not account to anyone, gives to someone, is an injustice, and that's it. I would also like to explain how those stocks came about. There is often speculation that taxpayers' money is here, that the Government has given something. I would like to make it very clear that at the very beginning after the restoration of independence, the authorized capital of the LB was actually formed by the Government. https:/ 3/8 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVito Vasiliauskointerviudienrasiui "Verslozinios",2014 04 30 l Lietuvosbankas But the basis of the contribution was formed not by money, but by buildings. Here, where we sit, at Gedimino Ave. 6, this the building was a contribution. Part of the financial assets of the Bank of Lithuania, i.e. gold, were inherited from the smetoninis Bank of Lithuania. And foreign exchange reserves were formed by the purchase of foreign reserves and foreign currency by the Bank of Lithuania. It's a big part - the result of the functioning of the currency board established by the Law on the Reliability of the Litas, when the demand for litas is increasing was satisfied by the purchase of the base currency- the euro. If we compare our reserves with those of other EU countries, including members of the euro area, we can see that our level of foreign reserves is far from high. Verslozinios", 2014 05 281 Lietuvosbankas LietuvosbankovaldybosnarioMariausJurgilo interviudienrasiui Verslozinios",2014 05 28 2014-06-03 Marius Jurgilas, a member of the Lithuanian Bank's Management, is interviewed by DaliusSimnas. Interviewpublished on 28 May 2014 in the daily newspaper "Verslozinios" - It has been a year since you joined the Board of the Bank of Lithuania (LB). What were the goals set for you and what did you manage to achieve? One of the main objectives is the introduction of the euro, and one of the main areas of curation is the cash service. In addition to the delivery of collectible coins, I am also responsible for the smooth introduction of the euro, for the banks to contribute to its introduction, so that there are enough places where the euro is exchanged. - What is the current downward trend in cash in Lithuania related to? m, from, It was only after talking about the euro that the amount of cash began to decrease. I would call this trend standard at the time of the introduction of the euro. History shows that if the central bank does not take measures, that amount of cash in circulation can fall to 40% from the previous level. Estonia's experience shows that a significant decrease in the amount of cash after that returns to its former level . However, such a fall is unhelpful for the Bank of Lithuania and, at the same time, for the State of Lithuania and its people, as it forces the sale of long-term investment positions, which reduces our reserves of international reserves. The Central Bank requires commercial banks to hold minimum reserves. But banks currently hold more than the supervisor requires, which means that banks have too much free funds. If we were to ask the banks, they would say that they do not see particularly great opportunities for where to invest those funds. Although the economy is recovering, the pace of recovery itself is not fast. Banks do not want to finance anything, so the amount of deposits is strong, which leads to the fact that banks have a lot of free funds. To manage this situation, the Bank of Lithuania 1/4 03/08/22, 14:57 Interview of Marius Jurgilas, Member of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, to the daily newspaper Verslo zinios, 281.05.2014 Bank of Lithuania took action and resumed deposit auctions of term bank maturing banks on May 6. The aim of this measure is to: reduce the surplus of litas in banks. - If the loan market is not gaining momentum in any way, then in the real estate (RE) market we are seeing a certain intensification, maybe you are already seeing new market bubbles? The Bank of Lithuania does not officially publish real estate market forecasts, but I can share the insights of the European Commission - real estate prices in Lithuania are projected to increase by 4%. - This is a very similar growth rate to that projected for the Lithuanian economy. Consequently, you do not see overheating Characters? The Bank of Lithuania has no problems with changes in real estate prices, at the moment the trends do not scare us. But we are closely following the real estate market and, if necessary, we will take measures. We note that there has been a significant increase in the volume of transactions, but the change in prices is not reflected in that increase. On the other hand, surveys of market participants conducted by the Central Bank show that expectations, which also lead to price changes, are improved. Until now, there have not been many residents who think that housing prices will rise by up to 20%, and now the share of the population who thinks so has increased. - And what would you explain about the fact that residents are currently more active in buying real estate from their own funds than they are financing transactions with borrowed money? Could it be that the money that was lurking in the shadows is now being invested in real estate? There are various conspiracy theories. And one of them would say that before the introduction of the euro, people are trying to change their cash savings to something more specific, such as real estate. And whether this theory is just a rumor or a truth, we do not have such data. But real estate is only one of the categories of wealth. There are many other types of assets in which it would be possible to invest funds. However, real estate is more attractive due to the fact that part of the transaction can be implemented in cash. - Will it not be the case that people who have actively invested before the introduction of the euro will take and be frustrated by those investments because of the failed expectations? Here I would like to make it very clear that real estate is not a good long-term investment. Centuries of data show that real housing prices (excluding inflation - Vz) do not change. Investing in housing is a good protection against inflation, but that's all. There are periods when real estate prices are rising, there are time sections when they fall, but in the long term, such investments will not help you accumulate large funds in old age. - The Bank of Lithuania has recently proposed to financial institutions, including payment and electronic money institutions, to develop an alternative payment system administered by the Central Bank, which would make interbank settlements and local transfers in euro cheaper. At the same time, you argue that success will depend on those involved https:/ /www. lb.lt/lt/kai bos-interview-p ristatai/lietuvos-ba nko-board-member-maria us-j urgilo-i ntervi u-dien rasei ui-versl o-zi nios-2014-05-2 8 2/4 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybosnarioMariausJurgilointerviudienrasiui Verslozinios",2014 05 281 Lietuvosbankas in the system. Have you already received a reaction from market participants? Why is this necessary, what is the essence of this proposal? When Lithuania joins the euro area, we will have to close the real-time litas settlement system LITAS-LRS. Target2, the only real-time euro settlement system, will remain. This means that Lithuanian banks who want to make real-time transfers without remaining in litas of the system will have to do so more expensively through the transfer system in euros, where the transfer costs EUR 0.8. As a result, siOlome banks will benefit from an almost real-time settlement system for the internal market from 2015 onwards, in which banks wishing to participate will be able to transfer funds to each other at a rate of EUR 0.1. Those funds will not be credited immediately, but quickly enough, for example, within an hour, or even more often, if participants so wish. High-value payments in euro will have to be made mandatory through TARGET2, but lower-value payments could bOti be made cheaper through the retail payment system for local payments. Indeed, we have heard such a request from the banks themselves, but there is currently no common solution. It is necessary, first of all, to hear an answer from the banks themselves whether they are interested in such a decision. In Estonia, which adopted the euro, the national retail payment system did not exist, while in Latvia the payment system EQF continues to operate. - Will these proposals lead to a decrease in the rates of local orders that are commonplace for bank customers? All payment systems in Lithuania will have to comply with the SINGLE EURO Payments Area standard by 2016. It was agreed with the banks that, in order to ease the administrative burden on them, they would not be required to upgrade their payment systems until January 2015, but only a year later. This means that for another year, the retail payment system that residents use to make local orders will be in place. However, in order to create the preconditions for reducing the prices of transfers to the end user, the Bank of Lithuania also sent a decision to financial institutions on how to reduce the fees for institutions that decide to participate in this system. Currently, this fee is 0.19 Lt (0.055 EUR), which is from 2015 we will reduce it about six times, to 0.01 EUR. This will allow us to reduce by about a fifth the rate of local online transfer, which is currently about 1.20 LTL for clients. - Would that mean that local commissioning on the Internet would cost up to 1? We provide an opportunity to make payments cheaper, and what the prices will be will be decided by the market itself. - And who needs all this, after all, bank customers can still make transfers cheaper in other payments today Institutions? ristatai/lietuvos-ba nko-board-member-maria us-jurgilo-interview-dienraseis-verslo-zinios-2014-05-2 8 3/4 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybosnarioMariausJurgilointerviudienrasiui Verslozinios",2014 05 281 Lietuvosbankas In this way, we encourage competition. Today, the same payment and electronic money institutions on legal restrictions can not directly participate in the payment system, so they make payments with the participation of the bank. The possibility to participate in the payment system of the Bank of Lithuania for all financial institutions will increase competition opportunities and in the market for electronic transfers. None other than consumers would benefit most of this. Other on the other hand, we still have large-scale cash payments in Lithuania. Compared to Estonia, Lithuania twice more settlements are made in cash. The system is stuck in such an unhealthy balance. Banks hoped that if the rates were raised to LTL 8 for the cash transfer, people would not do it anymore, but the cash the scale of settlement did not decrease. They migrate to other payment institutions that have kept rates low and there stuck again. Most of the cash payments take place at the post office, at the "Perlas" terminals, other payment points. The market needs to be helped to find a solution to this. And we hope that our proposal will help from that because individual market participants will not be able to find a solution. ristatai/lietuvos-ba nko-board-member-maria us-jurgilo-interview-dienraseis-verslo-zinios-2014-05-2 8 4/4

Title: Interview to the daily newspaper Lietuvos inios
text: 03/08/22, 14:57 rt, U.S. 11::)BANK LietuvosbankovaldybosnarioMariausJurgilointerviudienrasiui . Lietuvoszinios",2014 07 01 l Lietuvosbankas LietuvosbankovaldybosnarioMariausJurgilo interviudienrasiui Lietuvoszinios",2014 07 01 2014-07 -04 LinaMrazauskait is interviewed by LinaMrazauskait. Interviewpublished on 1 July 2014 in the daily newspaper "Lietuvoszinios" - The Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, who signed the agreement with VU, noted that economic science in Lithuania is receiving complaints, allegedly disconnected from reality. And how would you assess the state of science? - The situation of economic science in Lithuania, in my view, is very poor - there is a vacuum here. It is an eloquent fact that last year there was no one to award the Vladas Jurgutis Prize, established by the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, although there were a lot of candidates. At the moment, science is only imitated, having turned into a parody. In my opinion, economists who would print serious scientific works , form the scientific thought of Lithuania, can be counted on the fingers of the hands. m, from, - Universities of specialists in economics scienceprepared by the mathematics. How did it happen that there is a shortage of talented scientists preparing serious scientific work in Lithuania? How arethe countries that have avoided their shortage? - While working at a Norwegian bank, I learned that there is a special program in this country, according to which every year 5-7 of the most talented young people are invested: if they enter the five best economic universities in the world, their studies are fully funded, they are consulted, etc. The state knows that after 6 years, after the end of their studies, these people will return to Norway and become professors at the local university. In our country, there is a lack of such an approach. In Lithuania, even very serious, well-regarded private universities have decided not to invest in science, because this does not generate money. However, one thing is forgotten: without investing in science, we do not create a foundation, which subsequently allows us to achieve a high level of teaching . 1/3 03/08/22, 14:57 Marius Jurgilasinterviudienukuras of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania,01/07/2014 J Lietuvosbankas In 20 years, the majority of professorships and lecturers in Lithuanian universities have not changed. These people grew up in the old system, only a small part of them managed to break through, for example, began to read international literature. As a result, the quality of work undoubtedly suffers. Let's imagine that a motivated genius young man joins University of Lithuania. Years go by, he reads notes from textbooks of the last century, and his potential colleagues or competitors abroad at that time listen to lectures by top-level professors. Naturally, Lithuanian students have doubts about whether it is worth attending lectures instead of working, or whether it is worth studying in Lithuania. - So the problem is the quality of the studies, not the lack of motivation of the students? - I once asked tomas Venclova, a famous professor of Semiotics of Lithuanian nationality, who works at Yale University in America and sometimes teaches in Lithuania, how study systems differ in these countries. He replied that motivated and promising young people, who are very well trained and have a large baggage of knowledge, join Vilnius University, where they worked. Meanwhile, in America, students who have just joined tend to be like white sheets of paper. And yet, the main difference is that after four years of study, Lithuanians become specialists of the same or lower level than students who have completed their studies in America. Unfortunately, this situation has been the case in Lithuania for many years. - Is there a way out of this problem? Do you feel the changes approaching? - I think "tectonic fractures" are maturing in the study system. Small changes will no longer be enough - you need to fundamentally break it. Currently, the system focuses on a larger flow of students, as this generates higher incomes for universities. Consequently, the bar is lowered. Meanwhile, the professorship is encouraged to teach as much as possible and, due to the inhumane workload, does not get involved in scientific activities. What's more, in most cases, students are taught internships who only teach what they know, not what students would need. I am therefore convinced that universities should spend much more money on exploiting their scientific potential, although this may seem pointless to them. All the more so because there can probably be no better period than there is now for the popularization of economic science. After the economic crisis that has just existed and continues, interest in alternative economic theories is probably the highest in history. Currently, there are also many people interested in how the banking system works, how central banks behave, and so on. Moreover, the social security system in Lithuania has changed. All this attracts the interest of people, but no one conducts serious analysis on these topics. Opinions in the media alone are not enough. - Perhaps Lithuania and not need their own economics scientists - we could refer to the theories and insights of world-class scientists? - Foreign scientists, professors, lecturers visiting universities is an acceptable practice, but you also need to have your own. There is a need for science luminaries to attract young people of initiative. Then the scientific potential would begin to grow, to flourish. https:!/www. lb.lt/lt/kaibos-interviu-p ristatai/li etuvos-ba nko-board-member-maria us-jurgilo-interview-dienraseis-lietuvos-zin ios-2014-07 -O1 2/3 03/08/22, 14:57 Marius Jurgilasinterviudienukuras of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania,01/07/2014 J Lietuvosbankas The Bank of Lithuania is also interested in the presence of promising scientists in the country. At the moment, he feels great lack of high-level economists to hire for analytical work. Worldwide central banks, as the makers of important decisions, cooperate with universities that carry out various economics studies and prepares suitable specialists. And in Lithuania, no one undertakes such research, and this work lies on the LB, which does not always have the resources for this. That is why we decided on a complex solution. - You emphasize attracting economics scientists from abroad. Is the brain drain a big problem in economics science? - Definitely. In addition, there is a lack of guarantees for those who have gone abroad and want to return to Lithuania. I myself, having completed my doctoral studies abroad, wondered why not return to Lithuania. One university at that time offered me to sign a contract for six months. And then what? It is not known that everything will depend on whether the course is formed. Quitting jobs in America and returning to such uncertainty didn't seem wise to me. No promising scientist has an interest in taking risks for the vague prospects on offer - he needs to offer more. - Tell us more about the cooperation agreement and the function of the future Research Centre. - We hope that this Research Center will increase scientific potential, provide resources for long-term research, hold conferences, etc. In order to bring people of the appropriate education back to Lithuania, we will offer them the opportunity for scientific activities. And they will satisfy the analytical needs of LB in return. For the university, meanwhile, these people will help as researchers in the fields of economics, finance, banking. In other words, we will offer the departed Lithuanian specialists security - one foot to stand at the university, the other at the central bank. We will also try to be open, accept people and carry out short-term projects. We will also encourage LB employees to get involved - we want to give them the opportunity to break away from the routine, read the scientific literature, delve into problems that may be spinning in their heads for a long time, but it takes time to get out of them. After all, in order to answer serious questions, we need to collect data, conduct surveys, etc. For example, why is structural unemployment in Lithuania 1O% and what should we do about it? Why is 81% of payments made in cash in Lithuania and half as many in Estonia? We cannot expect answers to such questions in one day' time. - When will the Research Centre start its real activities? - Formally, the research center opens on July 1. But only in the autumn we will begin to look for scientists, we will try to convince them to return to Lithuania. Unfortunately, things are moving very slowly in this area. It is likely that these people, due to their obligations to teach at foreign universities, will be able to start working not immediately. . lb.lt/lt/kaibos-interviu-p ristatai/li etuvos-ba nko-board-member-maria us-jurgilo-interview-dienraseis-lietuvos-zin ios-2014-07 -O1 3/3

Title: Speech on enlargement of the euro area to Lithuania
text: 03/08/22, 14:43 ffl'I:) LI.ETUVQS B,AN KAS VitasVasiliauskas. Speechon enlargementof the euro area to LithuaniaI Bankof Lithuania VitasVasiliauskasS. peechon enlargementof the euro area to Lithuania 2014-07-22 (check against delivery) Eurofestivities2014 - enlargementof the euroarea to Lithuania Councilof the EuropeanUnion 23 July 2014, Brussels Ladies and Gentlemen, Dear Colleagues, It is my great pleasure to greet today so many of Lithuania's good friends. m,of 1 I believe I can call you this. Not only because you found time to join us for the event. But also because - or rather because - we have been together in less festive circumstances as well. For this reason many of you are familiar with Lithuania's economy no less than we ourselves. And therefore, I will not spend time sharing memories about the severity of the crisis. Or how hard we had to tighten our belts and clench our teeth in order to emerge with the achievement and satisfaction that is today - I very much hope - bilateral. We - the Lithuanian party - are happy to receive the official invitation, which at the same time is an official confirmation that our European orientation is focused, consistent and - irreversible. This message keeping in mind our geographical location and current geopolitical situation - is all the more relevant. 1/2 03/08/22, 14:43 VitasVasiliauskas.Speechon enlargementof the euroarea to LithuaniaI Bankof Lithuania I presume that today's decision is equally good news for the inviting party as well. The euro area and the Banking Union are receiving a partner that is financially disciplined, responsible and - credible. That has been proved. I mean both - during the recent five years and by our long-term monetary policy developments. 20 years ago - in 1994 - Lithuania established the currency board regime and in 2002 pegged its national litas to the euro. During the two decades we saw two dramatic shocks - the already forgotten Russian rouble crisis in 1998 and the recent global financial turmoil. And despite severe crunches and the following speculation, we have proven our abilities and commitment to maintain a stable exchange rate. Euro adoption is the logical next step that will ensure even greater confidence in monetary policy, financial stability and contribute to steady economic growth. Let me conclude by remembering a fresco that one can find in the Sainte-Pierre-le-Jeune church in Strasbourg. In this fresco, Lithuania is portrayed [according to the real factual data] as the last nation in Europe's march to the cross and Christianity. I sincerely hope and wish that in the history of the euro, Lithuania will not be the last. Here I would like to make it clear: I do not identify religion with money. But nevertheless these two marches in my view have one thing in common - they both lead to deeper integration and, as a result, bigger benefits for us all. Thank you all fellow-travellers in this journey. *** Attention to colleagues in Vilnius that watch our event! Now it is time to launch the clock starting the countdown to the euro in Lithuania. 2/2

Title: Speech on the Euro Conference Lithuania  Single Market, Single Currency, Common Future
text: 03/08/22, 14:42 VitasVasiliauskas.Speechon the "EuroConferenceLithuania- SingleMarket, SingleCurrency, CommonFuture" I Bankof Lithua... ffl'I:) LI.ETUVQS B,AN KAS VitasVasiliauskasS. peechon the "EuroConference Lithuania- SingleMarket,SingleCurrencyC, ommon Future" 2014-09-25 Goodmorning,dear LadiesandGentlemen, It is a great honour to welcome you to the Euro Changeover Conference. By accepting our invitation, today you are, in a way, part of a premiere - the first event accomplished by Lietuvos Bankas and the European Central Bank together. I believe you will enjoy the result. But, before we dive into discussions, let me share the latest news from my institution. This morning we welcomed a very distinguished guest. Mario Draghi, the President of the ECB, presented Lietuvos Bankas with the Euro Star - a symbol confirming that the national bank of Lithuania has been accepted into the euro family . Thank you, Mario, for the message. Q1 of 1 To be precise - thank you for the big message that covers so many aspects and that is, given the current geopolitical risks, all the more relevant today. Recently a foreign journalist asked me "What does the euro mean for Lithuania?" and suggested an answer : "Does entry into the eurozone mark the completion of disconnection from Russia?" He was surprised when my answer was "no, this does not mark disconnection from Russia". Disconnection was decided on and marked a quarter of a century ago. The euro in Lithuania confirms that our decision then was firm and final. Our European orientation is consistent and irreversible and we are ready,willing and fully prepared for deeper EU integration. . om1/4 03/08/22, 14:42 VitasVasiliauskas.Speechon the "EuroConferenceLithuania- SingleMarket,SingleCurrency,CommonFuture"I Bankof Lithua... Dear Colleagues, I have just mentioned "integration" - one of the key words that most likely will be in the air for the next few hours. To make sure that nobody gets lost in translation, let us stick to the classic definition: integration bringing together, combining into an integral whole. Not one joining another, not one blending into the rest, but clearly and definitely coming together into a whole. Consequently, integration is not a sponsor-recipient, or patron-ward relation, but a two-way traffic and a deliberate and dutiful partnership in it. I will be open. We are often asked about the benefits for us of adopting the euro. But very rarely about what we will bring to the club. As bankers we know that there are two sides to a coin. So, how do the two - the inviting and the invited - parties benefit from this deal that will be sealed in less than 100 days? This time, let me start with the inviting party. Reviving growth, boosting competitiveness, safeguarding financial stability - these are the top three tasks for the euro area today. And, in my view, Lithuania has good potential to contribute to getting ahead in all three directions. I will speak in facts: Lithuania is one of the fastest growing economies in the EU. It will be one of the fastest growing in the euro area as well. After taking into account the impact of the recent trade restrictions, we forecast 2.9 per cent real GDP growth in 2014 and 3.3 per cent next year. And, most importantly: these numbers are neither the consequence of good luck, nor of some base effect. We are adopting the euro from a strong and sustainable basis, exceeding the pre-crisis level of output without any major imbalances and cyclical gaps. The second good news - the euro club will be joined by a member that ranks no. 17 among almost 200 countries in the latest World Bank's Doing Business report. If we were to look closer, Lithuania is 3rd in terms of this competitiveness index among euro area members. And, finally, the euro area is gaining a partner that is financially disciplined, responsible and credible. During the past two decades we faced and successfully addressed several dramatic shocks - including the recent financial turmoil. And, despite unprecedented turbulences and the related speculation, we have proven our ability to successfully function under the fixed exchange rate regime. .. 03/08/22, 14:42 VitasVasiliauskas.Speechon the "EuroConferenceLithuania- SingleMarket,SingleCurrency,CommonFuture"I Bankof Lithua... As a central banker and supervisor of Lithuania's financial sector, I would also like to add that we will enter the Banking Union with a well-capitalised and transparent banking sector. It has not only dealt with its fragilities during the recent years, but also has accumulated twice as much capital as is required and nearly all of it is of the highest quality. Turning to the other side of the coin, for us the attractiveness of joining the single currency is obvious. By reducing the remaining frictions and barriers in the economy, the euro will have a visible effect on foreign trade. The elimination of foreign exchange risk and the expected positive effect on Lithuania's credit rating, will also lead to lower borrowing costs to non-financial corporations and households. Moreover, given better access to liquidity support for the financial sector in times of stress, the euro means increased resilience to shocks and more stable crediting environment. All this implies that the euro is a natural and important step to our further economic convergence. Dear Colleagues, Big changes are always surrounded by myths or prejudices. That is the rule. Therefore, it is no surprise that such a grand change as currency reform is also accompanied by both big expectations and worries. To be honest, I am not very worried about worries. They help concentrate for any exam, including the currency changeover. The experience of our neighbours, the Estonians and Latvians, also suggests that the fears will disappear shortly after the 1st of January when we find out that our national identity did not change, prices did not explode and we did not lose, but on the contrary - gained a voice in monetary policy matters by taking a seat at the ECBdecision-making table. However, I feel obliged to warn against the positive myths. The euro gives us many opportunities. But, big opportunities go together with big temptations. This is why now, after reaching the euro, we need even more self-control and financial prudency. To keep it short staying on the track of self-discipline is a key prerequisite for long term success. The euro is not an aim in itself. It only opens a big window for big opportunities. Their realisation depends on us. Ladies and gentlemen, .. 03/08/22, 14:42 VitasVasiliauskas.Speechon the "EuroConferenceLithuania- SingleMarket,SingleCurrency,CommonFuture"I Bankof Lithua... Let us be realistic - Lithuania is not a heavyweight player that can change the weather on its own. But if we take Estonia, Latvia and us together, I strongly believe in our potential to make a change. Lithuania's entry to the euro area completes the entry of the Baltic region as a whole. Being the last in the region and - at the moment - the latest entrant in the euro area reminds me of a medieval fresco in the Sainte-Pierre-le-Jeune church in Strasbourg. It portrays Lithuania as the last pagan European nation that accepted Christianity. I sincerely hope and wish that in the history of the euro the picture will be different - Lithuania will not be last. And, speaking as a central banker, in the coming decades, we will no longer need to make a distinction between the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks. Thank you.

Title: Speech by Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania at the opening of the Euro Exhibition
text: 03/08/22, 14:42 Speech by Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairmanof the Boardof the Bankof Lithuania at the openingof the Euro ExhibitionI Bankof Lithua... ffl'I:) LI.ETUVQS B,AN KAS SpeechbyVitasVasiliauskasC, hairmanof the Board of the Bankof Lithuaniaat the openingof the Euro Exhibition 2014-10-14 Palaceof the GrandDukesof Lithuania,23 October 2014, Vilnius Dear Guests, I am happy you were interested in and found time to come to our .... meeting. I should admit, just a few seconds ago, I had a doubt about how I should call it. A festivity? A celebration? Or,actually, a working session? a, of 1 Most likely, it is a festivity . Thanks to our host, we have gathered in a building which has the spirit elevating each and every Lithuanian above the everyday routine . On the other hand, we have gathered here to learn, to memorise, to prepare. Which means - for work. Today, in this beautiful palace, we have everything, and I hope and wish for every one of us to get what he or she has come for : beauty (it is abundant here), entertainment, and benefit. Which means knowledge. The survey data suggests that more than 20 per cent of our population have not seen euro banknotes yet. And 80 per cent know about them or at least have seen them . I should mention one obvious trend here: many of those who know the euro already support its introduction in Lithuania . While more than half of those who have not seen the euro, do not want it or are cautious about it. I should say it is normal for a human being, and even wise, to be cautious of what you do not know. Nevertheless, it's even wiser and safer to find out what it actually is. 1/3 03/08/22, 14:42 SpeechbyVitasVasiliauskas,Chairmanof the Boardof the Bankof Lithuaniaat the openingof the EuroExhibitionI Bankof Lithua... This is why we are here today. We, the Bank of Lithuania, in cooperation with our partner - the European Central Bank, will do our best for the euro - Europe's single currency, which is already used by our neighbours, the Latvians and the Estonians, and by more than three hundred million Europeans, to become well known, to become home currency for to us too. In order to make this process as smooth and simple as possible, and to avoid unnecessary tension or stress, we are launching an official information campaign today. In a few minutes my colleague from the ECB,Mr. Ton Roos, and me will open an exhibition which will mark the start of this campaign, and will be one of the major and, I have no doubt about it, most attractive channels to learn more about the euro. You will find both interesting and practical information in this exhibition. You will have a chance to see euro coins from other countries. You will learn what to do when receiving your change in the euro. Moreover, you will learn how to tell genuine euro banknotes from counterfeit ones. If anyone has heard people speaking about a need to buy a new wallet for fitting euro banknotes, you will be able to try your own wallet here. I was assured that a team of specially trained guides is very knowledgeable" and would be able to answer all questions from the visitors. We will see it ourselves soon. By the way, I would like to point out that this exhibition may be attended free of charge not just today, on its opening day. The exhibition will be open to all children and adult visitors until January 5. We are sincerely thankful to the Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania, its director Vydas Dolinskas and all his excellent team for such a possibility, for, I should say, a luxurious venue, benevolence and co-operation in organising the exhibition. On behalf of my colleagues and myself, I would like to thank the ECB which has already seen and participated in the process of euro adoption in 18 countries, and which has shared its euro introduction experience with Lithuania. Thank you, Ton. Dear all, Before coming to meet you here, I checked my working calendar at the Bank of Lithuania once again. And I can assure you, we are almost ready to adopt the euro. We have already minted more than half of the euro coins featuring Vytis, a treasured emblem of the Lithuanian state. They are kept in the Bank's vaults, waiting 2/3 03/08/22, 14:42 SpeechbyVitasVasiliauskas,Chairmanof the Boardof the Bankof Lithuaniaat the openingof the EuroExhibitionI Bankof Lithua... for their way to life to start. The euro banknotes are also arriving. The rest part of the work - to meet, to know, and to accept them - has to be done together with you. Thank you for joining us in that wok today. I wish you an interesting and useful afternoon. Euro adoQtion 3/3

Title: Interview to the portal LRT.lt
text: 03/08/22, 14:57 ffl'l:) LI.ET UVQS B,AN KAS LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVito VasiliauskointerviuportaluiLRT.lt, 2014 10 21 l Lietuvosbankas Interview of Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Lithuanian Bank Administration, forportalLRT.lt2, 014 1O21 2014-10-22 Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, is interviewed by Edgaras Savickas. The interview was published on 21 October 2014 on the portal LRT.lt - There's been more talk about lately the poor state of the world economy. The trouble is that the tools used during previous crises today usually no longer works. There is no longer an interest rate cut where - they are already almost zero. Increase the number of states costs also do not go away, because everyone immediately says: look at the deficits. Devalue currencies does not pay off, or even impossible (euro area case), because if everyone did it, then no one wouldn't win from international trade because everyone can't have a positive export/import relationship. You attended the International Currency last week m1 of 1 at meetings of the Foundation (IMF) and the World Bank. You may have heard some new suggestions there to resolve the situation, new approaches? - To describe in a few sentences all the discussions that took place during the meetings would be difficult enough, but it is possible to try to put together several directions . It is a fact that the economy is growing, especially if we talk about the global economy. There is no debate about this. Growth is also planned for next year (for this year - 3.3 percent, for the next - 3.8 percent). The question is whether it meets expectations . To this day, the situation is such that the forecasts are adjusted to the negative side . There are several reasons or explanations for this, there are certain unknowns. Economic cycles in individual countries of the world do not coincide. As for the US and euro area economies, they are different. The monetary policies pursued by central banks are also different. Therefore, to talk in this place about common recipes for the whole world would be naive and impossible to do at all. Recovery is stated, and at the same time it is stated that it is very fragile . One of the reasons for this fragility 1/6 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVitoVasiliauskointerviuportaluiLRT.lt,2014 10 21 l Lietuvosbankas there is a burden of debt that has naturally developed in both the private and public sectors. Second factor - the uncertain international situation, geopolitical factors, if we talk about Europe and Lithuania in particular. The eastern neighbors factor works more clearly than obvious. The purpose of the discussion was to find that middle ground. In principle, there was agreement on discipline, on compliance with the rules in Qeigu we would refer specifically to the euro area, it is the Stability and Growth Pact) and, at the same time, a strategy for flexibility in the expenditure side. That is, if investments are made, they must be made in a very targeted way, there must be high-quality costs, revised so that they provide added value. The third aspect is credit development. We are talking here about the euro area - how to make the steps taken by the European Central Bank (ECB) in the area of monetary policy pass into the real economy. Without a doubt, the executive branch has to do its job. These are structural reforms, and at least the position of the representatives of the central banks was very simple: monetary policy alone will not solve all the problems, a complex is necessary here. That is, the executive is doing its homework (structural reforms), while monetary policy, which now applies so-called unconventional measures in the euro area, is fulfilling its functions. When those two directions overlap, a result can be expected. Let's look at the euro area, which experienced growth after a fall of 6 quarters, but then again fell into some stagnation. It is stated: recovery is present, but very fragile. It is impossible to find some kind of common recipe for each state it is different. - More specifically, there is such a clash between France and Germany, along with the IMF. France is saying that we will reform when we can borrow more, or if you lend it to us, and we can spend more. At that time, the overseers, and with it Germany,say that no - you will first carry out structural reforms,and then we will lend it to you. It seems that,with such a skirmish, neither side can make progress. - I will certainly never comment on specific states. I can comment on Lithuania. It would be rude to comment on others because I don't think someone has as much information as that state itself. However, I have already mentioned that we in Europe have a Stability and Growth Pact. These are the rules that we have agreed on and must be followed. Why, then, to make an appointment? Why sign them? We have already had a situation once, about 1O years ago, when the great powers violated the rules. If we are now heading towards the same situation or a similar situation, then I think that is the problem. In this case, my position is categorical: there are rules and they must be followed. - I have no doubt that there would be opponents saying that the rules are bad. 2/6 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVitoVasiliauskointerviuportaluiLRT.lt,2014 10 21 l Lietuvosbankas - Then let's change the rules. In my opinion, they are not bad, because the name itself is the Stability and Growth Pact - it's not like you cut everything there and sit down. This is not the case. How in that saying what comes first - money or chairs (allusion to the novel by the Russian writer llja llf . Twelve chairs" - LRT.lt). I think first the chairs, then money. - In the US, you have also met with FEDvice ChairmanStanley Fischer, who has been very positive about Lithuania's efforts during the financial crisis. Mario Draghi, the head of the ECB, who recently visited Vilnius, also spoke in a similar way. You may remember the resounding quote of AndriusKubiliaus that the way Lithuania coped with the crisis will be written in the way in which Lithuania has overcome the crisis. I didn't notice that such would have appeared ... - Valdis Dombrovskis, former Prime Minister of Latvia, now Vice-President of the future European Commission, wrote a book about their exit from the crisis . How Latvia has overcome the financial crisis." I would see many analogies with Lithuania. - Betar you agree that Lithuania's actions, the belt-tighteningpolicy, were legal? - When your gross domestic product falls in the 15th, when there is a debate about your insolvency, in my opinion, you will do your best to correct that situation. That was done. There was simply no other alternative. As a result, there were 9 prae. consolidation, both by raising taxes (I stressed VAT) and by abandoning certain costs, was the only way out of the crisis. That worked, we already reached the pre-crisis level last year, and now we are already driving forward. For such a small, frankly, export-oriented economy, I think that was the right way to go. The only alternative was the devaluation of the valiant. By the way, some authoritative international institutions offered this to our Latvian neighbors. - You say that Lithuania was in a situation where there was an increase in emigration, an increase in unemployment, and the implementation of these decisions, were not avoided? - Economic indicators confirm this. When I hear it said that the global financial crisis was caused by local banks, it makes me laugh. It's just that that was the objective reality. Or when they say that the crisis was caused by nightly tax reform - this is how people who are simply unintelligible or do it for political purposes can speak. The markets showed very clearly what condition our economy was in at that time. 9 prae. the interest rate clearly identified the risk premium that we had to pay for the economic situation at the time. Doing nothing would have meant only a deterioration of the situation. In my opinion, in principle, the decisions have been made the right ones, although the details can certainly be debated. In the tax field, certain aspects can be discussed, but the direction was unequivocally the right one. - Whether Mr Kubiliaus's name will end up in the economics - will show, but today it is probably clear that your name as LBvadov, who introduced the euro in Lithuania in 2015, should appear in the textbooks of theistory. How do you feel about that? 3/6 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVitoVasiliauskointerviuportaluiLRT.lt,2014 10 21 l Lietuvosbankas - You see, the activities of the Bank of Lithuania in the euro adoption project are purely related to the emergence of a new currency. It's more than that I would emphasise the focus of our activities on the euro as a means of payment. In addition to joint work with the executive a government project would be impossible. It was a strategic goal of the government, so I don't see anybody here the exclusive role of the LB. It's just a job. I would say that this will certainly contribute to the further integration into the European economy. I believe that this is a good prerequisite for economic growth. I stress - Assumption. This took place alongside other works - both the arrangement of the banking system and the change in the model of maintenance. Itself I wouldn't see a special thing in that. Yes, we will have the euro, which I see as an opportunity, a chance for Lithuania. Cuddly that I was in time and place. - You say it was a job. After all, the person of anyprofession, having done the work, feels in some way. Do you feel good about the work you've done? - Yes, because if I didn't feel good, I wouldn't work here. - I'd like to go back to U.S. current affairs. FeDtap's recent gossip in the media after one of his former employees made public secretly made records revealing that there was a fairly frivolous look at the regulation of one of the banks- GoldmanSachs. Could something similar happen in Lithuania? More precisely, what is the LB's situation with regard to the banks? - We have a supervisory mandate and we are implementing it. The approach to the banking system and individual banks is simply that of the regulator. We do not give anyone any privileges, exceptions, we do not make special conditions. Our experience of all the years of operation shows this. If we see the problems that exist, we solve them. Starting. Snoru", .Farm Bank", as well as in credit unions. I think we're acting as a fair arbiter. I am completely calm in this place. If the question was whether we could be expected to avoid any problems in the future, my answer would be unequivocal - no. You can never expect anything. Such a life, there is no statics here, only dynamics. No one is immune from encountering criminal matters, and the overseer is not a law enforcement agency. Law enforcement usually goes from behind, so no one is immune from the criminal greed that exists, as we know not only from international examples, but also from Lithuanian ones. I can tell you that we have done, we are doing and we will do our best to avoid problems in the banking sector and in the financial sector in general. Our mandate mandate mandates that we do this. - Do those L Gdprbuilders who take up supervision work every day in LBpastatear's bank branches? - Routine work takes place in the LB, work with data, their analysis, risk assessment. But there are also special actions - inspections when going to the outside, to the subject you are inspecting and performing control actions in it. It's a combination of two kinds of work. 4/6 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVitoVasiliauskointerviuportaluiLRT.lt,2014 10 21 l Lietuvosbankas - From next year, the three banks operating in Lithuania (Swedbank, SEB and DNB) will enter the ecb directly upkeep. Are you ready for this transition? How will it go? - Without a doubt, we are connected to this process. Formally, we will only join the banking union from the date of membership of the euro area, i.e. from 1 January next year. At that time, the banking union itself starts from November 4 of this year. However, in Lithuania, an assessment of the assets of those three banks has been carried out. We, as a supervisory authority, have been involved in those processes. And in the future, it will be a joint work with the ECB to monitor the entire banking system, including those three largest banks. It is not the case that they are removed from our banking system and are supervised exclusively by the ECB: it is a joint effort. Especially since the mothers" of these banks are outside the banking union. There will be such a trinitarian system here, where Scandinavian supervision, we and the ECB, will take part. It is true that the ECB will have direct responsibility. The goodness of the Single Supervisory Mechanism is that there will be the same standards for the largest banks in the euro area. No one has ever done such an exercise, when the bank's assets are assessed in principle, the portfolio is redrawn. The European Union will be the first to do so. - This exercise is currently taking place? - Yes, it is ongoing, and the results will be announced on October 26. Throughout that period, we have seen very obvious facts: European banks have seen more than EUR 200 billion in aid. strengthened its capital. I think that's really good news. - You have also already started your work on the ECB Governing Council yourself. Starting from the New Year, you will also acquire a decisionright. I know that very many people would like to know what your position is on interest rates - to reduce it further, to leave the same, maybe to increase it? - These are matters of monetary policy that are discussed in the governing council. Meetings are currently held at the first meeting of each month. From next year, there is a transition to a six-week cycle (the same as the Fed). The rule is that those things are unnotated. I certainly wouldn't want to be the kind of person who would break these rules. Today, the direction is very clear. There is a shift towards unconventional monetary policy measures. What the interest rate cut to a minimum was what happened in June and September. As well as the adoption of other incentive measures - the granting of longer-term loans, the announcement of programs for the acquisition of various types of securities, which should start soon. All this suggests that the ECB, through monetary policy, is trying to influence the economy so that the liquidity provided to the banks reaches the real economy as soon as possible, and the economic recovery so sought is achieved so that it accelerates. How it works out - let's get older, we'll see. However, I would like to emphasise once again that, among others, 5/6 03/08/22, 14:57 LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVitoVasiliauskointerviuportaluiLRT.lt,2014 10 21 l Lietuvosbankas there will be nothing in the performance of the roles of the actors. We each have to do our job. - If the recent stock buyback program didn't work out, do you think it should be expanded or abandoned even more? - There are several programs today. Let's start with what is published. First of all, these are targeted long-term financing operations in which loans to banks are provided for four years. Then there's the asset-covered securities program and the asset-based bond program. They are published and should begin. We'll see what their influence is. For now, it would be difficult to talk about what would happen if there were. The reaction of the financial markets is determined by a whole series of factors, and these programs are just one of them. Trust is a very important factor. Apparently, everyone hopes that with these unconventional means it will be possible to direct money to the real economy. - I understood from this conversation that you would most like it to be the governments that take on more responsibility and undertake structural reforms. - My point was that we each have to do our job. If we point fingers at each other, nothing will happen. Central banks do their job, executive authorities - their own. That is why I say that structural reforms and unconventional monetary policy decisions act as a mixture that can serve a breakthrough. 6/6
