Verslozinios",2016 06 231 Lietuvosbankas Interview of The Republic of Lithuania's GovernmentlordialoTomas Garbaraviius to the daily newspaper "Verslozinios", 23/06/2016 2016-06-23 The Lithuanian Bank's ManagementLordleTomas Garbaraviius is interviewed byJustinasGapsys.Interviewpublished in the daily newspaper "Verslozinios" on 23 June 2016 and on the portalVZ.LT23 June 2016. - Why exactly now did LB talk about the risks of the SwedishNT? Are there any signs that the real estate bubble is fading or is about to start to fade? Even after recognizing that there is a bubble on the market, it can still blow for a long time. Which scandinavian real estate marketindicators are causing the problem? The Financial Stability Review of the Bank of Lithuania is published by who years and one of the goals of this review is to name Potential emerging for Lithuania's financial system Risks. If we see risks, we need to inform the public about them. The risks associated with m1 of 1 with the ongoing increase in house prices in Sweden, we first mentioned back in 2011, at the moment it is one of the the most pressing risks to lithuania's financial system. Perhaps even more relevant than the risks associated with a long period of low interest rates. These effects accumulate and increase over time, for example, during the acceleration of housing creditworthiness and the ensuing potential pressure on house prices. Last year, the main risks were related with geopolitical tensions, sanctions imposed by Russia, and it is gratifying that it did not manifest itself in the way it could possibly have manifested itself. When this risk subsides, the main one, in my opinion, is the risks associated with the situation in the real estate markets of the Nordic countries, especially in Sweden. It is difficult to estimate its size, but at the moment it is the most relevant. The day before we published the Financial Stability Review, the Riksbank, the Central Bank of Sweden, also published its Financial Stability Review, which also highlights swedish real estate price risks. Their the tone of the press release is also quite strong. We did not coordinate (tone - Vz), but it coincides. Nothing amazing, because the Riksbank has been concerned for some time now and is urging the other authorities to take all measures. From 1 June, the so-called amortization requirements came into force in Sweden: for borrowers it will no longer be enough to pay only interest, j ie will have to amortize part of the loan as well, at least up to fifty percent 03/08/22, 14:55 Interview of The Board of the Bank of Lithuania byarioTomas Garbaraviius to the daily newspaper "Verslozinios", 231.06.2016 Lietuvosbankas housing values. Thus, the Riksbank is also concerned about the high level of household indebtedness and the ongoing rise in house prices. In this regard, the preparation of banks is being strengthened (for an unfavorable scenario - Vz), which is what it's important to us, too. Before the crisis, our banks were heavily indebted and were receiving money from swedish parent banks. They do not have such a source and receive a significant part of the funding from wholesale markets. Thus, the loan portfolio of banks is growing rapidly and borrowing from wholesale markets, which are not the most stable source of flunance. On the other hand, it should be noted that Swedish banks are more capitalised than other banks in Europe and in terms of the supervisory capital adequacy ratio. - However, in the Financial Stability Review it was mentioned that the capital ratios of Swedish banks are close Minimum. The capital buffer they have, or the excess of the required capital adequacy ratio, is not very large, but what is important is that sweden has a number of macroprudential instruments in place, so-called capital buffers, which can be used if necessary. They are designed to build up reserves in good times, let's say 'axial', that can be used in times of crisis. Thus, swedish banks' capital surpluses are not significant, but mainly because capital protection, systemic risk and systemically important institution buffers are applied. the Swedes were among the first to apply these bumpers and are among the most conservative in their application. - How would the impact on Lithuania manifest itself if swedish real estate risks materialized? The review says that during the withdrawal of money, but at the same time it is reassuring that banks operating in Lithuania are no longer so indebted to banks in Sweden. The obligations of banks operating in Lithuania to parent banks (in jargon they are often called mothers) are significantly reduced and amount to about 11% of the total flnansation. Banks are fleeing with local resources, and that's welcome. The risks in question are no longer so important either because banks can always take advantage of the euro system's reflection operations, which they can increase liquidity by providing collateral. So, from a liquidity point of view, the risks are, I would say, much less. From the point of view of capital, one can see risks that are difficult to assess and that are associated with a possible decrease in crediting. At the moment, the banks are paying out dividends, but they had accumulated "bacon", which they would hardly have been able to lend quickly, i.e. use to cover the risks of new loans. Even after the payment of dividends, a fairly solid excess of capital remains. Banks need capital surpluses to be able to credit. If you do not have an excess of capital, you cannot lend either, because every new loan "eats" the excess of capital. In other words, the excess capital indicates the ability of the bank to increase the loan portfolio. - So it can be interpreted that the need for parent banks to strengthen their capital through dividends is already working on the lending opportunities of banks operating in Lithuania? 2/4 03/08/22, 14:55 Interview of Tomas Garbaraviius, Member of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, to the daily newspaper Verslo zinios, 231.06.2016 Bank of Lithuania In view of the past surplus of capital, the dividend disbursement that has taken place is, I would say, to be regarded as completely natural the reallocation of capital within banking groups. It would certainly have taken years for the banks to have borrowed the excess capital they had, so there is no logic in holding that money (here the Vz). Let's not forget that Swedish banks after the crises had contributed additional capital. Now they have gotten out of the losses they have suffered, they have begun to make a profit. If you look at the balance sheets of some banks and look at the prospects for the lending market, you can see that their capital was with a really big margin. Therefore, I would not interpret the dividend disbursement that has taken place as a capital strengthening for parent banks. Swedish real estate price risks may not manifest themselves - the so-called hardball does not necessarily have to happen landing, because both as a result of the actions of the authorities and without them, a smooth and painless one can occur soft landing. However, we must warn that a bad scenario is also possible. - Do you have at least hypothetical calculations of what is the appetite of the local market to borrow, how much banks are able to lend, and according to this - how much dividend can be paid out? In previous years, the banks' forecasts were somewhat too optimistic. They - the entire banking system - did not borrow so much. This year, banks are forecasting a 7.5% growth in the loan portfolio. According to our estimates, based on the results of the first quarter, the three subsidiaries could collectively still pay out a dividend of about half a billion euros. That's how much they could pay out to still meet the minimum capital requirements, but there would be no more room for credit. If we include the results of the stress tests, which show how much capital the banks would need to cover potential losses, then the amount that can be disbursed would be reduced to EUR 0.35 billion. Eur. - Taking into account the fact that Swedbank paid out 491 minutes at one time. Eur dividends, not so much and a lot of money left payout? As a rule, we do not comment on the results of individual banks, but in this case it is clear that a significant surplus of capital has been accumulated, which would probably have been difficult to recruit quickly in the form of an increase in the loan portfolio. In Lithuania, corporate lending has finally recovered, but it is difficult to say whether the modest annual growth rate of the loan to companies portfolio is more a matter of demand or supply. As far as we ask companies, they say that banks are reluctant to lend, and when asked by banks, it turns out that they want to lend, but do not find good companies. However, it seems that the two sides are getting better and better together, and the question now is how many good projects there are that could be financed. In general, Lithuanian companies borrow relatively little from banks - the financing provided by the capital banks of northern Europe in the structure of the flnansification of companies currently accounts for only about 11%. Most of the use is made of own funds, shareholder loans, trade credits and other sources of fluncy. Thus, a significant lack of financing from banks is difficult to see. When studying the trends in the disbursement of bank dividends, it should also be taken into account that at the moment banks are profitable and replenish the available excess capital every year. 3/4 03/08/22, 14:55 Interview of Tomas Garbaraviius, Member of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, to the daily newspaper Verslo zinios, 231.06.2016 Bank of Lithuania - Perhaps your assessments of credit growth are too conservative, given how quickly wages are rising, how are housing transactions increasing? Maybe this will lead to more active borrowing, and for this the necessary capital in the banks will no longer be available at that time? Mortgage lending has indeed intensified, and it is gratifying that the changes we have made to the Responsible Lending Regulations have not affected crediting, and that is what we were aiming for. Additional macroprudential safeguards have been introduced, but mortgage lending continues to grow. Housing prices are rising no faster than the salaries of the population. Corporate lending has also recovered, and at the moment the annual growth of the loan portfolio for companies is already positive again. Banks, especially large ones, declare that they want to lend to smaller companies. The cash flows of such companies, of course, are changing more, their history of operation is shorter, but banks assure that they want to lend to such companies. We will look in the coming years at how much that portfolio will actually increase and how banks' capital surpluses will change. At the moment, the banking sector does not appear to lack capital to increase its loan portfolio. - By what means, in addition to the payment of dividends, banks operating in Lithuania can strengthen the capital of parent banks? Dividends are the main instrument that Swedish and Norwegian banks are likely to use to redistribute capital within groups. It is also important that, if the situation worsens, in order to have additional free capital, northern European capital banks in Lithuania can reduce risk-weighted assets, first of all by reducing credit to riskier borrowers. A decreasing volume of crediting would slow down Lithuania's economic growth. Financial stability, Banks, Swedbank, AB 4/4

Title: Commentary  about Lithuania's membership in the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank
text: 03/08/22, 14:54 Commentary by Marius Skuodis, Director of the International Relations Department of the Bank of Lithuania, Delfi.It about Lithuania's membership in the Asian infra... 11). LITHUANIAN LEARN BAN direktoriausMariausSkuodziakomentarasDelfi.It of the Department of International Relations of the Bank of Lithuania on Lithuania's membership in the AsianInfrastructure Investment Bank 2016-08-29 The month of Lycoon, during which Lithuania can still decide to become a member of the AsianInfrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB). Membership in the new international development bank in the future would open the door for this Beijing-based investor to finance specific Lithuanian projects. At the same time, it is likely that Lithuanian business would gain better Opportunities participate Implementing Bank funded projects in other countries. The Bank's activities are already being attended by our Polish neighbours, all Q 1 ish 1 Scandinavian and the major EU countries, and more EU Member States are in line with new countries. But Lithuania is still not among the 57 founders or among those who have decided to join. Unfortunately, there is also no reasoned explanation as to why. Lietuvosinteresai At first glance, it may seem that the name of the AIIB, which opened in Beijing at the beginning of 2016, strictly defines the purpose of the bank - investment in the infrastructure of Asian countries. As a result, the question naturally arises, how is Lithuania related to this? However, the bank's managers stress that its name primarily reflects the largest shareholders, but does not limit either its region of activity and investment or its membership, so this opportunity has already been used by 14 EU countries that became the first shareholders of AIIB. 1/3 03/08/22, 14:54 Comment by Marius Skuodzias, Director of the International Relations Department of the Bank of Lithuania, Delfi.It about Lithuania's membership in the Asian infra... Together with them, Lithuania, having become a member of the AIIB, would gain the opportunity to participate in the creation of Eurasian infrastructure connections in the process, and the state authorities would gain an additional information channel about the political and economic processes. It is also important that Lithuanian business is actively looking for new opportunities in the Chinese market, and the country's institutions are consistently strengthening bilateral cooperation, Lithuania's membership in a new Chinese-dominated international institution could also have a positive impact on the development of bilateral relations with China. In this context, it is important not to forget China's interest in the transport, financial and other sectors of our region, where Lithuania actively competes with neighboring countries. Of course, membership in a new international institution would require additional contributions from the Lithuanian budget, the exact size of which is not clear today. It also has to be acknowledged that the bank is still in its infancy, which makes it quite difficult to quantify the potential benefits of membership. However, the question is why, even in acknowledging and appreciating the uncertainty that exists, other EU countries are rushing to this institution so much? And why Lithuania did not really even consider China's invitation to become a bank founder? The worldview has changed: anxiety is replaced by support China's initiative to establish a new international financial institution was initially met with caution in the world. The U.S. and Japan reacted particularly sharply, fearing that AIIB would adhere to lower standards than the World Bank or the Asian Development Bank when financing projects (the World Bank is dominated by the United States, and the Asian Development Bank by Japan). Nevertheless, the most important U.S. allies in Western Europe - the United Kingdom, France and Germany quite quickly accepted China's invitation to contribute to the initiative. The original provisions of the EU Member States have also changed dramatically. When the Chinese government announced the initiative to set up a new international development bank, eu countries had informally agreed on possible membership to consult each other, but when the deadline announced by China came to an end, it turned out that as many as 14, i.e. exactly half of the EU countries, individually decided to become the founders of AIIB without coordinating their intentions with each other. Despite the cautious initial reaction, today the US, Japan, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank and other international institutions also support the activities of the AIIB. In addition to supporting the bank's operating principles such as "management efficiency" and "the highest ethical and environmental standards", the opportunity to cooperate in sharing the risks of financing specific projects in the region is particularly attractive to all parties involved. 2/3 03/08/22, 14:54 Commentary by Marius Skuodzias, Director of the International Relations Department of the Bank of Lithuania, Delfi.It about Lithuania's membership in the Asian infra ... The ongoing shift in economic power to the East Of course, when it comes to the development of Lithuania's relations with Asian countries, Lithuania's strategic interest - the greatest possible integration into Western structures - should not be called into question. At the same time, however, today it is no longer possible not to notice the shift of world economic power to the Asian side. Many analysts alone recognize that the establishment of the AIIB is perhaps the largest tectonic breakthrough in the world's financial architecture since the founding of the IMF and the World Bank in 1944. Another event illustrating the consolidation of China's growing international role is that since October, there have been 100,000 new cases. the decision to add the Chinese currency yuan to the IMF's reserve basket will come into force. The latter is used in the financial relations of countries with the IMF,but so far it contained only the US dollar, the euro, the Japanese yen and the British pound sterling. With the inclusion of the Chinese currency, the weight of other currencies will decrease accordingly (unfortunately, the euro will be the most numerous). Finally, this year, China, which holds the G20's club of the world's largest economies, has already outperformed the U.S. in the competition for the status of the world's largest economy. According to imf data, in 2015. China's share of global GDP in purchasing power parity was 17.1, the US was 15.8, and the total EU(still with the United Kingdom) was 16.9 prae. True, one can always argue about the interpretation of the statistics, but the trend is obvious: although in the 1980s there was a great deal. China's share of global GDP in purchasing power parity was only 2.3 prae., the IMF forecasts further growth for China, which is expected to reach as much as 19.4 prae in 2020. Meanwhile, the role of the EU and the US in the global economy, according to forecasts, will continue to decline by almost 1 prae in the same period. Point. In view of the ongoing trends, Lithuania's decision on membership in AIIB largely depends on the answer to one fundamental question - whether Lithuania is determined to move more firmly towards an increasingly active role Region? If this decision does not seem obvious now, then in the medium term the approach will most likely have to change. So, would it be more prudent, taking into account all the factors, to take this strategic step in a timely manner, that is, to join the founders now, instead of humbly asking in the future for an accepted and persistent effort to seek membership? 3/3

But please don't worry: I promise to stick to the programme and won't even try to tell you the whole history of this special landmark . Nevertheless, I would like to highlight the striking similarity between the forces that transformed this location and the forces shaping trade and economic growth nowadays. a, is1 The Palace of the Grand Dukes has its roots in a small settlement in the 6th century. Both political and economic linkages propelled it forward from its modest initial stages into a national administrative and cultural centre in the 16th_17thcenturies. Similar to how our economies evolve, the Palace was initially built with local labour and materials . As its dwellers needed to perform more diverse and sophisticated functions, the Palace incorporated more specialised labour and refined materials. Historians make us aware of Polish craftsmen, Italian architects, German engineers and Hungarian decorators. Sandstone for the floors was imported from Livonia (current Latvia) and Sweden, metalwork - from Poland and Austria, glass - from France... The closer political and administrative regional integration required stronger economic cooperation. Title: Interview to the news agency BNS
text: Interview of Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, to the news agency BNS, 06/03/2017 Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, is interviewed by sarunas Sabaitis. The interview was published on March 6, 2017. -Sometimes it seems that traditional banking in Lithuania has occupied defensive positions. How do you see her future? "In my opinion, traditional banking is coming out of the trenches, it's also changing. Already last year, we were able to feel a certain breakthrough, as demonstrated by the reaction of the banks to the instrument of the main account, the so-called basket of services. New technologies, competition really have an impact, which is why the banking sector is also opening up to innovation. Banks in general open up, get out of their separatist cages and try to think about a common standard, a common proposal, consider how it will be necessary to live in a new environment. That's why I'm looking at traditional banking in a reasonably positive way -- I think the tipping point is in the past and things are changing now. -In the matter of the basket of services, banks also scrambled only after receiving a request from the Bank of Lithuania to provide the main account service. This did not show a great desire to take the initiative yourself. "You know, it's hard to get out of your comfort zone." When you feel good, you have secured some kind of return, you get a stable income, which devils do you get out of your comfort zone? However, banks are no longer closed, and this is due not only to the actions of the Bank of Lithuania - I would put more emphasis on new trends and the development of innovations. Several factors need to be considered - new players, new technologies, the self-awareness of the banks themselves and the activity of the regulator (Bank of Lithuania -BNS). For example, with regard to the area of payments, the Bank of Lithuania was probably the first to start talking back in 2011 that something was maturing here and that there would be changes. Banks are also rethinking their actions, assessing whether something has been missed, looking at global trends, and finally, what is happening to the Scandinavian banks that manage them. Everyone understands that there are new opportunities here - New opportunities also require new investments, but at least some banks have not actively carried them out in recent years and have paid out sufficiently large dividends. "I look at it simply enough." For Scandinavian banks, Lithuania and other Baltic states are a home market, so cash flow management, their walking inside a banking group is a normal thing. We live in the European Union, in the conditions of the free movement of capital, so there is no problem for capital to either leave or come. "Don't you think that the behaviour of the banks was also influenced by their somewhat arrogant imagination?" "I think for sure, but again, I'm seeing a good change. I don't want to pre-empt, but at least from our interactions with banks, we really feel it. Yes, there were those arrogances in the past, but now I definitely see good prospects. "What led to such a picture of banks?" The absence of real competition? -There were shortcomings in the implementation of the mandate for market supervision of the provision of financial services. I would like to remind you that it came into the hands of the Bank of Lithuania only in 2012, so it took us a few years to start moving that water. Of course, there was a lot of discontent, we ourselves are learning how to behave in that porcelain shop, but now there is more and more mutual understanding. We do not want something exclusive, we see banks as partners, we want the penetration of electronic services to be as wide and high as possible. Society will be better off, we as a regulator will be better off, and finally the banks will be better off because they will achieve economies of scale. Everyone will be able to live happily enough and wait for a bright tomorrow. "The commercial banks themselves sometimes stay away. For example, for SEPA payments, most of them chose not the decision of the Bank of Lithuania, but a less attractive instrument of Scandinavian banks for customers. "I think it was a business decision that was also influenced by the cost issue - it's cheaper to form a whole group-wide traffic. But yes, Lithuanian customers were used to a better standard, and through there (Scandinavian banks -BNS) they got a worse standard. There's that nuance, I think not really everything should be seen in money. The banking business, as I understand it, must look at least from the perspective of three to five years. The client needs to be invested so that he uses the services provided more widely and can earn more from it in the future. - Banks do not invest in customers, they fight for them - among themselves, with credit unions, with payday loan companies. Didn't that become the reason why the emergence of alternative market players was overlooked? "I don't think the banks haven't noticed the emergence of new players. We are talking about a global trend, and the new intermediaries came to finance perhaps last. Direct contact, the expulsion of the mediator from communication, first began in the public sphere. Facebook, uberization, all that sharing economy has finally come into finance as well. The reaction of the banks, they missed those processes or did not miss them, could not prevent it. "Still, there's a sense that the banks' reaction was overdue. -As I said -comfort zone effect. In addition, the consequences of the crisis, let's face it, were certainly considerable for the banks, it was necessary to deal with loan portfolios, provisions, borrowers. The banks had something to do. "The current economic cycle, the low interest rate environment, also have an impact on banks' behaviour?" "Without a doubt." As we may see, the main source of income for a classic universal bank is interest. The low interest rate environment has a direct impact on banks' performance, especially if the financing costs are relatively low, then it is difficult enough to squeeze that margin. When new intermediaries, innovations in fintech, are contributing to all this, we have to review our entire business model to see if it works properly. In my opinion, this is precisely one of the reasons for the merger of Nordea and DNB banks, that is, the attempt to ensure returns, the points of synergy, primarily in the area of costs. But I believe that the banks will remain the main players in the credit market for a long time to come, at least in Europe. Of course, banks will remain the main players in the deposit market, as our deposit statistics show. Of course, alternatives also appear here, various (peer-to-peer or crowdfunding -BNS) platforms are being established, but the population's habits are also changing slowly, we are conservative people. There are a lot of factors influencing here, let's not forget about the deposit insurance factor. "It's not uncommon for banks to argue their stock behavior with stricter regulation, new requirements that also require additional investment. "Yes, but where did the economic crisis start, isn't it from the financial sector?" This is a new reality, and in the European Union we must talk about consolidating the entire banking sector. It requires more capital, tighter regulation, but those are the new rules of the game. You take part in the race, you withstand or do not withstand, you will not do anything. - Bank consolidation is also taking place in Lithuania, it does not pose a danger to consumers? -There are those consolidation trends - last year Swedbank acquired danske bank's retail business, this year Nordea and DNB banks intend to complete the transaction. I would see it purely as a search for business efficiency and synergy. Consolidation in the sector itself is certainly not a bad thing, it is important that it does not increase concentration and does not reduce competition. In the main segments, such as the loan market, competition is now sufficient, in other areas there may be some signs of concentration, but that is what we are, there is the Competition Council, we supervise that whole market. We are definitely seeing the arrival of new players in the market - electronic money institutions, payment institutions, (peer-to-peer or crowdfunding -BNS) platforms. - Commercial banks often complain that the requirements imposed on them do not apply to new market players. "Most of the new players in the market are not banks, naturally the conditions are different for them. Of course, equal treatment and equal treatment are our mandate and in our blood, but we cannot apply the same regulation to the fly and the elephant, but as far as the supervision of financial services is concerned, the prevention of money laundering - there are no exceptions here. What I would like to emphasize - we have such a sandbox mode. Let's say a technologically new and innovative player is coming, sometimes not even knowing for himself what it will be like in three years. It's also a new thing for us as a regulator, so we're putting him in a kind of lab and training both him and us. Someone may see that we are creating some kind of greenhouse conditions, but this is not the case, we are trying to understand what can grow out of that green mass through the beasts. And in this place we are not something new -- the caretaker of England does the same thing, the Scandinavians do the same. The better an understanding of business models we have, the better it will be for everyone. By the way, banks are now also facing up to innovation, and their innovation units are working with a laugh. I only see opportunities for cooperation. - Lithuania presents itself as a payment center, in this area it actively seeks to attract Chinese investors. What determines such a position? -Lithuania is a small but ambitious and hungry country. As a member of the euro area, you can do everything that other euro area central banks can do, but in order to compete, you have to do something differently, you have to stand out in something. I believe that relations between the European Union and China have a perspective, trade relations develop dynamically, and where there is trade, there is also financing, there is payments. Why can't Lithuania be a point between the two reserve currencies in the area of payments? That's what we're working on. "Maybe there are already some specific results?" We have letters of intent, we see the steps of individual payment institutions, but we also need to understand the differences in mentalities. We think and plan actions in years, and in the East and ten years is a short period of time. Maybe in terms of time, we were too much optimistic imagining that we would have a result soon. But I think that in the next few years we will be able to boast that in the area of payments, the point of connection between those two reserve currencies is in Lithuania. - Other countries probably have similar ambitions too? -The Chinese actually work with a lot of things, Lithuania is only one of the possible ports for them. We're watching, we know who those competitors are, and we're working hard enough to realize that. -Poland has received a number of investments from China's financial sector, including traditional and investment banking. -Usually the banking sector goes after customers. Chinese companies are active in the Polish market, which makes it interesting for Chinese banks as well. This is the state policy of China. We are too small for the Polish model to work for us. We can only be mediators, and that is something that we should all understand. On the other hand, in China, government and business go hand in hand, so cooperation between the Lithuanian authorities and the Chinese authorities is very important if we also want economic cooperation. - In the past, another strong commercial bank was expected to come to Lithuania. Can we already give up such hopes? "Let's be realistic, the Baltic market is not large, so we could expect exactly those new innovative players, mobile, online banking to come to our countries. -One such player is British Revolut, which has declared its intention to obtain a specialised bank licence. How is he doing? "We know, they're still in the stage of intent. He's interested, but he's not advanced yet. The idea of a specialized bank is really attractive, we definitely have more interested in it. Our specialists almost weekly accept interested people from foreign countries who are interested in the possibility of setting up a business in Lithuania and developing it throughout Europe. The number of contacts with us has increased several times, especially when it comes to investors from abroad. "When can you expect not only interest, but a breakthrough?" -We see that the news about Lithuania is spreading rapidly, we are recommended to our members by foreign financial sector associations, companies that have already received or are considering obtaining a license, we are receiving the attention of foreign media. At the moment alone, we have received and are dealing with 15 requests to set up fintech and other financial institutions that would compete in one way or another with traditional banks. More than half of them are foreign investors. Starting with Israel, Germany, Great Britain and ending with Singapore and other countries. There are even more fishing rods thrown. I think this year we can expect new players to come. "For now, banks have looked at new players more from a high point of view, but maybe it's worth looking for opportunities for cooperation as well, because in the future, both sides probably won't be able to do without each other? "The sooner we all go to the stage of cooperation, while realizing that competition is a natural thing, the better it will be for everyone. I think that understanding is coming, there will be enough space under the sun for everyone. Banks manage huge data flows, here there are unlimited possibilities for synergy. - But the initiative to create an instant payment system was transferred by banks in Lithuania to mobile operators. How can such a decision on their part be explained? -There are a few points that should be highlighted. Instant payments, at least in some Scandinavian countries, are a banking horse, but there, too, the population's habits are different than with us. In addition, many banks operate in all the Baltic states, not to mention the Scandinavian states, so it is difficult to find any horizontal solution, especially considering that in banking groups all processes are tried to be made horizontal and universal as possible. I would say that in this place, mobile operators are simply more flexible. Banks are also developing certain products on their side, they will be able to offer things like Bank ID, Smart ID and so on. Products are developed, ideas are developed, and thanks to the competition, the client will definitely win. Only, of course, one should talk about having one standard, because in such a small market as Lithuania or all the Baltic states, it is too expensive to create parallel structures, prices will become unattractive for the consumer. In the longer term, in the area of payments, in my opinion, everyone should be pleased if we are able to provide these services at cost. - It can be expected that the system being developed in Lithuania will become a common standard in Latvia and Estonia? "I think it would be in everyone's interest if we had some kind of horizontal solutions for all three Baltic states. "There are already specific steps in this direction?" -The good thing is that the same operators operate in all the Baltic states, on the other hand, it is easier to talk with Latvians and Estonians will be when we already have the product. So far, the testing laboratory is located here in Lithuania, and in the area of care, we are, without a doubt, cooperating with our neighbors. - And Latvia and Estonia are not developing similar projects? -Estonians do not have a national payment system, in Latvia it is, but it is more focused on the public sector. Yes, Latvians have ambitions in the area of payments, instant payments are a new thing in the whole euro area, there are many initiatives, we will see who gets here. -The services of new players are more focused on the young and innovative consumer. In your estimation, how long will it take for their wider prevalence? "We have a proven strategy for 2017-2020, in which one of the strategic goals is payments, their innovativeness. We have set a very specific goal - on average, one person now makes about 160 payments a year, our goal is to double this figure in 2020, and this is not the limit yet. We in Lithuania are actually very innovative, we have one of the fastest Internet connections, the electronic space is not alien to us, so we definitely see great potential. I think that in the medium term we can expect a breakthrough, I am an optimist. -New opportunities also lead to the emergence of new risks. "Without a doubt." New technologies relate, in particular, to cyber risks, to customer identification, to the admission of the non-bank sector, new intermediaries to payment systems. We see those risks, we are investing in preventing them, but I also have no doubt that we will have incidents as well. You need to prepare for this, not be afraid to communicate about it publicly, to be transparent in this place. "Money laundering issues are also probably very relevant?" "New players also mean changes in the prevention of money laundering. What used to often be outside the law, such as virtual currencies, is now slowly becoming a daily occurrence. We already have initiatives to amend the money laundering directive, which are also focused on virtual currencies. We are living in an interesting era, transformations are underway and what seemed unthinkable until yesterday is becoming a reality today. Could anyone have imagined five years ago that cars would be able to drive themselves? Probably not. It's the same with the financial sector, there's a revolution going on. If earlier we imagined that we were spectators in a cinema, now it is already necessary to realize that we are one of the actors. - Don't you think the legal regulation of new services is overdue? "The law is already there, it always comes from behind. Of course, it would be good to predict what will happen in the future and adjust everything in advance. Therefore, sometimes it is very important not to be afraid to improvise, to pre-empt a little. Sometimes you do not have to wait for European directives, no one forbids you to try to guess trends at national level and regulate what will perhaps be done in Europe in just a few years' time. Of course, there's a risk all the time that you're going to have to harmonize again, to replay, but whatever you do, that's life. - The Bank of Lithuania seeks to be proactive in this area? "Yes, we are trying to be proactive, we have clearly set ourselves the goal of cooperating with the financial sector, reducing the administrative burden, moving to the electronic space. Of course, it's not simple, because we have to change ourselves, but I think we'll succeed. Thanks for the conversation.

Be abejo, lygiateisikumas ir vienodas traktavimas yra ms mandate ir ms kraujyje, bet negalima vienodo reguliavimo taikyti musei ir drambliui, taiau kiek tai yra susij su finansini paslaug prieira, pinig plovimo prevencija -ia joki iimi nra. K noriau pabrti -mes turime tok smlio ds (anglikai sandbox) reim. Tarkime, ateina technologikai naujas ir inovatyvus aidjas, kartais net pats neinantis, kuo bus po trej met. Mums kaip reguliuotojui tai irgi naujas dalykas, todl tupdome j savotik laboratorij ir treniruojams -tiek jis, tiek mes. Kas nors gali velgti, kad mes sudarome kakokias iltnamio slygas, bet taip nra, mes bandome suprasti, kas per vris i tos alios mass gali iaugti. Ir ioje vietoje nesame kakuo nauji -Anglijos priirtojas t pat daro, skandinavai t pat daro. Kuo geresn verslo modeli supratim tursime, tuo geriau bus visiems. Beje, bankai  inovacijas dabar irgi yra atsisuk veidu, j inovacij padaliniai dirba isijuos.Aia matau tik bendradarbiavimo galimybes. - Lietuva save pristato kaip mokjim centr, i srit aktyviai siekia pritraukti Kinijos investuotojus. Kas lemia toki pozicij? -Lietuva yra maa, taiau ambicinga ir alkana valstyb.Bdamas euro zonos nariu, gali daryti visk,k gali daryti kiti euro zonos centriniai bankai, taiau nordamas konkuruoti, kak turi daryti kitaip, turi kakuo isiskirti. A manau, kad Europos Sjungos ir Kinijos santykiai turi perspektyv, prekybiniai santykiai pltojasi dinamikai, o kur prekyba, ten yra ir finansavimas, mokjimai. Kodl mokjim srityje Lietuva negali bti taku tarp dviej rezervini valiut? Ties ia sritimi mes ir dirbame. -Gal jau yra kakoki konkrei rezultat? Turime ketinim protokolus, matome atskir mokjimo staigingsnius, bet turime suprasti ir mentalitet skirtumus. Mes galvojame ir planuojame veiksmus metais, o Rytuose ir deimt met yra trumpas laiko tarpas. Gal laiko poiriu mes buvome per dideli optimistai sivaizduodami, kad greitai tursime rezultat. Bet a manau, kad per artimiausius kelerius metus galsime pasigirti, kad mokjim srityje jungimosi takas tarp t dviej rezervini valiut yra Lietuvoje. - Kitos alys turbt taip pat turi panai ambicij? -Kinai i tikrj dirba su daug kuo, Lietuva jiems yra tik vienas i galim uost. Mes stebime, inome kas yra tie konkurentai, ir t suvokdami pakankamai intensyviai dirbame. -Nemaai Kinijos finans sektoriaus investicij, skaitant tradicin ir investicin bankininkyst, sulauk Lenkija. -Paprastai bankinis sektorius eina paskui klientus. Lenkijos rinkoje aktyviai veikia Kinijos mons, todl ji domi ir Kinijos bankams. Tai yra valstybin Kinijos politika. Mes esame per daug mai, kad lenkikas modelis pas mus veikt. Galime bti tik tarpininkai, t mums reikt visiems suprasti. Kita vertus, Kinijoje valdia ir verslas eina kartu, todl ir Lietuvos valdios institucij bendradarbiavimas su Kinijos valdios institucijomis yra labai svarbus, jeigu norime ir ekonominio bendradarbiavimo. - Anksiau buvo laukiama dar vieno stipraus komercinio banko atjimo  Lietuv. Ar toki vili jau galime atsisakyti? -Bkime realistais, Baltijos ali rinka nra didel, todl mes galtume tiktis btent t nauj inovatyviaidj, mobilios, internetins bankininkysts atjimo  msalis. -Vienas i tokiaidj yra Didiosios Britanijos Revolut, deklaravs ketinimus gauti specializuoto banko licencij. Kaip jam sekasi? -Msiniomis, jie vis dar yra ketinim stadijoje. Domisi, bet toliau kol kas dar nepasistmjo. Specializuoto banko idja yra tikrai patraukli, besidomini ja tikrai turime daugiau. Ms specialistai kone kas savait priima interesantus i usienio ali, kurie domisi galimybe steigti versl Lietuvoje ir pltoti j visoje Europoje. Kontakt su mumis skaiius iaugo kelis kartus, ypa kalbant apie investuotojus i usienio. -Kada galima tiktis ne tik susidomjimo, o proverio? -Matome, kad inia apie Lietuv sparia plinta, savo nariams mus rekomenduoja usienio ali finans sektoriaus asociacijos, mons, jau gavusios ar svarstanios galimybia gauti licencij, sulaukiame usienio aliiniasklaidos dmesio. Vien iuo metu esame gav ir nagrinjame 15 praym steigti fintech ir kitas finansstaigas, kurios vienaip ar kitaip konkuruot su tradiciniais bankais. Daugiau nei pus i j usienio investuotojai. Pradedant Izraeliu, Vokietija, Didija Britanija ir baigiant Singapru bei kitomis alimis. Umest mekeri yra dar daugiau. A manau, iemet mes galime tiktis naujaidj atjimo. -Kol kas bankai  naujus aidjus irdavo labiau i aukto, taiau gal vertt paiekoti ir bendradarbiavimo galimybi, nes ateityje abi puss tikriausiai negals isiversti viena be kitos? -Kuo greiiau mes visi pereisime  bendradarbiavimo stadij, kartu suprantant, jog konkurencija yra natralus dalykas, tuo visiems bus geriau. A manau, kad tas supratimas ateina, vietos po saule uteks visiems. Bankai valdo didiulius duomen srautus, ia yra neribotos sinergijos galimybs. - Bet iniciatyv kurti momentini mokjim sistem bankai Lietuvoje perleido mobiliojo ryio operatoriams. Kuo galima paaikinti tok j sprendim? -Reikt iskirti kelis aspektus. Momentiniai mokjimai bent jau kai kuriose Skandinavijos valstybse yra bank arkliukas, bet ten ir gyventojproiai yra kitokie nei pas mus. Be to, daugelis bank veikia visose Baltijos alyse, jau nekalbant apie Skandinavijos valstybes, todl sunku surasti kok nors horizontal sprendim, ypa turint omenyje, kad bank grupse visus procesus bandoma kuo labiau padaryti horizontalius ir universalius. Sakyiau, ioje vietoje mobils operatoriai tiesiog yra lankstesni. Bankai savo pusje irgi vysto tam tikrus produktus, jie gals pasilyti tokius dalykus, kaip Bank ID, Smart ID ir panaiai. Vystomi produktai, vystomos idjos, o dl konkurencijos tikrai laims klientas. Tik, aiku, reikt kalbti apie vieno standarto turjim, nes tokioje maoje rinkoje, kaip Lietuva ar visos Baltijos alys, kurti paralelines struktras yra per daug brangu, kainos taps nepatrauklios vartotojui. Ilgesnje mokjim srities perspektyvoje, mano nuomone, visiems reikt diaugtis, jeigu pavyks teikti ias paslaugas u savikain. - Galima tiktis, kad Lietuvoje kuriama sistema taps bendru standartu ir Latvijoje bei Estijoje? -Manau, visiems bt naudinga, jeigu turtume kakokius horizontalius sprendimus visoms trims Baltijos alims. -Konkreiingsniia kryptimi jau yra? -Gerai yra tai, kad tie patys operatoriai veikia visose Baltijos alyse, kita vertus, lengviau kalbtis su latviais ir estais bus, kai jau tursim produkt. Kol kas bandym laboratorija yra ia, Lietuvoje, o prieiros srityje mes, be jokios abejons, su kaimynais bendradarbiaujame. - O Latvija ir Estija nepltoja panai projekt? -Estai neturi nacionalins mokjim sistemos, Latvijoje ji yra, bet daugiau orientuota  viej sektori. Taip, latviai turi ambicij mokjim srityje, visoje euro zonoje momentiniai mokjimai yra naujas dalykas, yra daug iniciatyv, irsime, kas ia gausis. -Naujaidj paslaugos yra labiau orientuotos  jaun ir inovatyv vartotoj.Js vertinimu, kiek prireiks laiko platesniam j paplitimui? -Mes esame pasitvirtin 2017-2020 met strategij, kurioje vienas i strategini tiksl yra mokjimai, j inovatyvumas. Esame usibr labai konkret tiksl -vidutinikai vienas asmuo per metus dabar padaro apie 160 mokjim,ms tikslas yra 2020 metais  skaii padvigubinti, ir tai dar nra riba. Mes Lietuvoje i tikrj esame labai inovatyvs, turime vien greiiausi interneto ry, elektronin erdv mums nra svetima, todl tikrai matome didel potencial. Manau, kad vidutiniu laikotarpiu galime tiktis proverio, a esu optimistas. -Naujos galimybs paskatina ir nauj rizik atsiradim. -Be jokios abejons. Naujos technologijos vis pirma yra susijusios su kibernetinmis rizikomis, su kliento identifikavimu, nebankinio sektoriaus, naujj tarpininksileidimu  mokjimo sistemas. Mes tas rizikas matome, investuojame  j prevencij, taiau a taip pat neabejoju, kad tursime ir incident. Tam reikia ruotis, nebijoti apie tai vieai komunikuoti, bti skaidriems ioje vietoje. -Pinig plovimo klausimai taip pat tikriausiai yra labai aktuals? -Nauji aidjai reikia ir pokyius pinig plovimo prevencijoje. Tai, kas anksiau danai buvo u teiss rib, pavyzdiui, virtualios valiutos, dabar po truput tampa kasdienybe. Jau turime iniciatyvas dl pinig plovimo direktyvos pakeitim, orientuot ir  virtualias valiutas. Gyvename domioje epochoje, vyksta transformacijos ir tai, kas dar vakar atrod nesivaizduojama, iandien tampa realybe. Ar kas nors galjo prie penkerius metus sivaizduoti, kad automobiliai gals patys vainti? Turbt ne. Tas pats ir su finans sektoriumi, vyksta revoliucija. Jei anksiau mes sivaizdavome, kad esame irovai kino teatre, dabar jau reikia suvokti, kad esame vieni i aktori. - Ar nemanote, kad nauj paslaug teisinis reglamentavimas vluoja? -Teis tokia jau yra, ji visada eina i paskos. inoma, gerai bt nuspti kas bus ateityje ir i anksto visk sureguliuoti. Todl kartais yra labai svarbu nebijoti improvizuoti, truput ubgti u aki. Kartais nereikia laukti europini direktyv, niekas nedraudia bandyti nacionaliniu lygiu atspti tendencijas ir sureguliuoti tai, kas galbt tik po keli met bus padaryta Europoje. Aiku, vis laik yra pavojus, kad reiksvliau harmonizuotis, peraisti, bet k padarysi, toks gyvenimas. - Lietuvos bankas ioje srityje siekia bti proaktyvus? -Taip, mes stengiamsbti proaktyvs, esame aikiai isikl tiksl bendradarbiauti su finans sektoriumi, mainti administracin nat, pereiti  elektronin erdv. Be abejo, tai nra paprasta, nes ir patys turime keistis, taiau manau, kad mums tas pavyks. Dkui u pokalb.

The interview was published on April 28, 2017, in the supplement to the daily newspaper "Verslozinios", entitled "Banks and insurance." Lithuanian banks seem to have already exhausted cost-cutting countries. Their administrative costs are increasing again as wages rise. How can banks increase profitability? What can you expect from them? What stood out in 2016 was that borrowing grew sustainably in all sectors - loans to businesses, consumer credits, housing loans to the population. We believe that these trends will continue this year. So further the growth of banks must be attributed to their classic activity - lending. m, from, We see that the banking sector is responding to the changing business environment, challenges for well-established businesses Models. Last year, the consolidation of banks took place, and competition is growing in the payment market. As for nordic banks, which occupy the largest share of the Lithuanian market, their return on equity is higher than in the rest of the EU. The average return of ESbanks reaches 3- 5%, and the indicator of Nordic banks - 10% and above. In Lithuania, the return on equity is even higher. I believe that these trends will continue in the future. How would you diagnose the appetite of market participants to borrow. It has grown,deteriorated? In 2016, the loan portfolio for companies grew by about 10%. After excluding a number of business merger transactions, which were financed by borrowed funds, the loan portfolio grew by 5.3%. When financing business development, own funds still prevail. We cannot say that companies are diving headlong into the credit market. We see some caution, primarily because of geopolitical factors. The uncertainty of the business environment remains, it does not add certainty to the business about the future, and this is understandable. It wasn't new to us and reactions like this, in my opinion, are normal. On the other hand, in 2016, the EU's subsidised projects have not yet fully taken hold. Is there a normalthis trend? Roach the accumulation will end? The bulk of deposits are only called deposits, but in fact these are cash funds on current accounts. Differently in words, it is not a means of saving or investing. Since the financial system is dominated by the banking sector, the population, companies naturally consider monetary funds Banks. There is no developed capital market in Lithuania. In addition, we are conservative, we are not inclined to choose alternative investment instruments. And all this leads to the fact that most of the money is in current accounts. I believe that we need to change behaviour, to look for other means of investment. Then the situation could change. You have mentioned the new players in the banking market. Can you reveal a bank coming to Lithuania? We are seeing a more intense interest in our market for several reasons. We have made it easier to enter our market, i.e. when setting up a so-called specialized bank, it is subject to a lower authorized capital requirement (1 min. Eur, when 5 min. Eur is usually required). Internet and mobile banks are being developed. Our desire to create a favourable environment for companies using modern financial technologies does not slip through the eyes of market participants. The Bank of Lithuania aims to make Lithuania a centre of financial technologies in the Nordic-Baltic region by 2020. As part of a common payment system in euro, access through Lithuania to the single euro area market is also tempting. So this interest hasn't yet become fleshy, but certainly more intense than it was in the first half of 2015 or 2016. This is natural, because the economic cycle is moving uphill. The pattern of banking activity has changed, so we can expect new entrants to the market. Whether they will fundamentally change the system when the market is concentrated in the hands of the three largest banks in Lithuania is too early to say. The Baltic states as a market are small, so if an investor comes, they will come because of the euro area and, in particular, because of the expected withdrawal of the United Kingdom (UK) from the Community. It is important for banks operating in the UK to maintain access to the eu's single market, and here I would see lithuania's niche. For which banks in Lithuania there is a requirement to have additional capital reserves, why, what is the reserve? Do banks comply with this requirement? We are talking about smaller, national banks. It is more difficult for them to compete because of their size. They focus on riskier segments. They also have historically established portfolios of assets, loans, which require capital strengthening. In addition, when the euro was introduced, banks lost part of the income from currency conversion - commission income for currency exchange. Thus, for a number of reasons, additional capital requirements are imposed on them. How do you assess that the housing loan portfolio has grown faster than the Lithuanian globalBVP? Will we not overheat? What further growth of the loan portfolio could be seen as dangerous? As for home loans, today we see that approximately every second transaction for the purchase of housing is financed by loans. It is clear that the crediting of housing transactions has increased. On the other hand, the Lithuanian housing market is not homogeneous. We have the capital Vilnius, the big cities and the rest of Lithuania. Price increases we see, but it doesn't mean anything in itself. Incomes are growing, the economic situation is improving, and therefore housing is also increasing prices, and for them to grow drastically, I could not say. Looking at the relationship with the country's GDP, we do not yet see that the situation is analogous to that in the period 2006-2008. We make evaluations on a quarterly basis. We will consider this issue in the fall. Then we will think about whether it is necessary to respond to the changing environment, to impose additional capital buffers on banks and thus to suppress crediting. Yes, we are seeing a change in the temperature of the real estate market, but so far we see no reason to take on additional Measures. The forecasts for such economic growth in Lithuania, as it is now, were not very expected, and the forecasts are being improved. What has not been appreciated by the experts? If this is related to the growth of the EU economy, what has not been appreciated by the experts in predicting the growth of the EU economy? This year, the Bank of Lithuania forecasts that GDP will grow by 2.6% - faster than in 2016, when growth of 2.3% was recorded and significantly more than the economy grew in 2015 (1.8%). A better economic environment in Europe affects us, our export markets, so it is only natural that our forecasts are more optimistic. In addition, EU support will have a greater impact on our GDP growth. On the other hand, we also see certain factors that can quickly change the situation. So far, the factors of the external environment hang in the air, have not been resolved, primarily geopolitical factors. What do you mean by geopolitical health? I am not talking so much about the East, but about the changes in normal international trade in general, about the steps of the new US administration: so far we have a lot of talk, a lot of deliberation, but there are no real steps. And Lithuania is an open economy, so we are and will be dependent on the international environment. Is the Greek factor, the debt issue, a list of risks hanging in the air? I think that's not the main factor, or as significant as it was in the past. Today, an agreement with the Greeks is approaching and, hopefully, there may be a new agreement on Greece in the summer. Finally, that agreement is needed because a new phase is approaching in the summer, relating to their debt, their creditors' claims in Greece. How much can it cost the EU economy and Lithuania to withdraw from the Community in the coming decade? Such calculations were carried out in the medium term. However, everything will depend on what kind of agreement is reached during those two years of negotiations. What will be the economic relationship between the EU and the UK, what will be the free trade agreement, whether it will be at all. All this will affect the development of the UK economy and the economic development of the rest of the EU, including Lithuania, in the medium term. For Lithuania, the direct influence will certainly be insignificant enough, mainly related to the pound rate. As we know, remittances from Lithuanians living in the UK reach the Lithuanian economy. But here we are talking about the influence of several decimal places. . lb.lt/lt/kaibos-interviu-p ristatai/lietuvos-ban ko-board-first ninko-vito-vasi liausko-interview-d ienraseiui-verslo-zi nios-2017-04-28 3/ 5 03/08/22, 14:54 LietuvosbankovaldybospirmininkoVito Vasiliauskointerviudienrasiui Verslozinios",2017 04 281 Lietuvosbankas Indirect influence, specifically on our exports, is, in my view, much more important. How much will the hard one respond or a milder Brexit scenario for the remaining 27 EU Member States, it will have such an impact on us as the British trading partners. You are a member of the Governing Council of the European Central Bank{ECB). The Council has taken decisions on the monetary policy of the euro area. How and when can the climate for land interest rates in the euro area change? It is clear that those interest rates will sooner or later start to rise. As far as interest rates are concerned, in my opinion, the European Central Bank, its Governing Council, represented by the central banks of the euro area, and we, too, have made our calendar and our directions clear. That is, the quantitative easing programme will run until December of this year. Therefore, talking about any movements in the field of interest is simply not worth it, because it would be inconsistent. First you need to finish the program, and only then think about the next steps of monetary policy. In our directions, which we are announcing, we make it clear that even after the end of the quantitative easing program, interest rate growth is apparently difficult to expect. Yes, today the economic situation is improved. Have we reached a tipping point? I think not yet. We need to wait even longer for the middle of the year, because on a monthly basis economic indicators vary greatly, especially inflation indicators. One month inflation is moving towards 2%, the next we have only 1.5%. Such instability, unsustainability, suggests that so far there is no basis for talking about a fracture. True, one is already clear. We have avoided deflationary price risks. This is a fact. I believe that a free monetary policy has contributed a great deal to this. Has there been a breakthrough? For now, let's wait. Does this mean that interest rates and the price of money will remain low for a long time? So. Apparently, it should be said that low interest rates will remain in the medium term. It is clear that by the end of the year the interest rate will not change. I don't think anything dramatic should happen next year either. How do you predict the potential changes in the exchange rate of the euro, the trajectory, what to expect for those exporting the US,Asian markets? The ECB and the euro system as a whole do not seek to artificially influence the exchange rate of the euro. The exchange rate of the euro is determined by international trade. The euro, as a reserve currency, reacts naturally to what is happening, but with significant changes in the exchange rate of the euro to one side or the other i wouldn't predict. Following the crisis of 2008, many changes have been made to the issue of banking supervision. Is it possible to say that we are fully prepared for a new possible crisis? If not, what might not work? A lot has been done, but not everything. As we know, the banking union is built on three pillars. The Single Mechanism for Banking Supervision has been in place since November 2014. I think he's getting in. There is a common mechanism for the resolution of banks, too, but I would point out here that we are still getting stronger, we are hearing initiatives about a kind of relaxation of the resolution mechanism, a desire to return to public funds to save the banks. We do not yet have a common deposit insurance scheme, so we cannot yet talk about the banking union as a completed project. There is no ideal situation. All the more so, history shows that the crisis strikes each time from a different angle. But the fact is that compared to 2008, the EU-euro area is stronger. At the beginning of April, in Malta, you discussed with the EU finance ministers and the heads of central banks the long-standing problem of non-performing loans, the proposals to set up a European bad bank asset management company financed by taxpayers' money. What is the opinion? The consensus was that a European structure should not emerge, but that national solutions must be sought to deal with the issue of bad loans. The differences of opinion on State aid have persisted. When the legislative document is submitted to the Council of the EU, there will apparently be some kind of compromise on this issue. The Bank of Lithuania and the Ministry of Finance do not support such proposals. Countries that have resolved the issue of bad loans, such as the Scandinavians, the same Croatia, take a similar position. In my opinion, this would run counter to the spirit of the Bank Resolution and Recovery Directive, which states that the banks themselves must also manage public finances, and public money should not be given to the rescue of problem banks. Those proposals concern the banking sectors of some southern European countries. We had the problem of non-performing loans, but we solved it by creating provisions for bad loans. So it would be a strange situation now that some countries have coped and others are not doing very well, and here again the states are going to the rescue. How do you see the perspective of the reform of the Pension System, what would the Lithuanian Bank advise the Government to reconsider? At the meeting of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania on 28 April this year, we are scheduled to consider it, and then we will make our proposals public. Our research center has examined the entire pension system in Lithuania with other bank experts. As well as the experience of foreign countries, especially when it comes to the countries of Eastern and Central Europe, with whose pension systems ours is most comparable. Of course, the fundamental issue concerns the second pillar of the pension system. We will come forward with our proposals, but it will take a great deal of political discussion and consensus for the pension system to meet public expectations. The fundamental problems that have a negative impact on the pension system are linked to demographic processes, that is, the shrinking ratio of the working population to the unemployed, as well as to the shadow labour market economy, those ills that could kill any, even the most ideal, pension system. Achieving some progress in these areas will make it easier for everyone. When those problems hang, everything else, in my subjective estimation, is just pushing the parameters without addressing the substance of the issue. It should be noted that a specialized bank differs from a regular bank not only in a lower minimum capital requirement, since it is subject to 1 min. Specialised banks will be able to provide the usual banking services - accepting deposits, providing loans, payment services, etc., but will not be able to engage in more complex operations, such as those related to derivatives or investment banking. The mere emergence of a new type of license does not increase the risks posed by the already new players entering the market. Another issue regarding the reputation of new foreign entities - here we are strict: reliable origin of capital, impeccable reputation of managers and shareholders, sustainability of business models are the cornerstones of entry into the Lithuanian market. text: 03/08/22, 14:37 ffl'I:) LI.ET UVQS B,AN KAS Memberof the BoardMariusJurgilasinterviewwith,,Verslozinios" I Bankof Lithuania Memberof the BoardMariusJurgilasinterviewwith ,,Verslozinios" 2017-08-04 PauliusCiuladainterviewsMariusJurgilas,Member of the Boardof the Bankof Lithuania.This interview was publishedon 30 July2017 inthe daily newspaperVersloiinios (VZ.LT). Whywas it decidedto invitemorebanksto Lithuania?Is this an initiativebythe Ministryof Finance,Bankof Lithuania,or the new Government? The Bank of Lithuania's strategic directions for 20172020 include becoming a financial sector partner a, of 1 encouraging innovations and sustainable growth and formation of a competitive and advanced payments market in Lithuania. The Bank of Lithuania aims at increasing competition in the Lithuanian financial sector : with growing numbers of market participants, there are newcomers offering more efficient and low-cost services, thus incumbents need to step up their game as well. The market of Lithuanian banks in Lithuania is relatively concentrated - 3 banks take up a major part of the market. But this isn't a situation characteristic of only Lithuania, as many small countries experience it as well. Therefore, we can be attractive to foreign market participants as a market first, through which 450 million people living in the European Union can be reached. The Bank of Lithuania proposed the idea of a specialised banking licence and prepared appropriate draft legislation - the goal was to increase competitiveness within the basic financial services sector. With approval by the legislative body, the possibility for credit unions to become banks was simplified, while easier establishment of banks drew the attention of new market participants . Recently we have been experiencing significant interest from really strong potential market players abroad . In particular, investors from Israel, Germany, China, Singapore, US, UK, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Sweden and other countries are interested in specialised banking licences. 1/2 03/08/22, 14:37 Memberof the BoardMariusJurgilasinterviewwith,,Verslozinios"I Bankof Lithuania The active work of the Bank of Lithuania and other institutions on publicising opportunities to set up in Lithuania is bearing fruit. We can clearly see that information on Lithuania's advantages has spread far and wide - we are recommended by foreign financial sector associations, other companies that have already received or plan to receive this licence; we garner attention from foreign media. In relation to reduction of the licence fee, in February 2017 the Bank of Lithuania, taking into account the actual cost of providing administrative services, presented to the Ministry of Finance a proposal on the recalculation of the licensing fee for banks from EUR 50,000 to less than EUR 5,000. Is there no riskthat easedrequirementswill attractto the countrybanksof a less-than-stellareputation? It should be noted that specialised banks differ from regular banks not only because of a lower minimum capital requirement - they have a EUR 1 million minimum capital requirement instead of the regular EUR5 million requirement applied to regular banks - but also in the range of services provided to customers. Specialised banks can also provide regular banking services - accept deposits, provide loans, payment services, etc., but they cannot engage in more complex operations, such as those related to derivative financial instruments or investment banking. However, both specialised and regular banks have to comply with the same supervisory requirements, including capital adequacy criteria, money laundering prevention requirements and other operational requirements. Butcriticsclaimthat easedrequirementswill attractweak banks,as strongplayersdon'tsee the capital barrieror licencepriceas an issuewhenenteringa newmarket? The mere appearance of a new licence does not increase the risks raised by new players entering the market. Regarding the reputation of new foreign subjects, this is a different issue and here we are very strict - the main criteria for entering the Lithuanian market is a reliable source of capital, impeccable reputation of managers and shareholders, sustainability of the business model. This is something we clearly state to potential investors as well. We also take appropriate steps internally at the Bank of Lithuania and dedicate resources to the assessment and management of risks raised by new participants. Title: Time to change the paradigm of cash
text: 03/08/22, 14:36 ffl'I:) LI.ET UVQS B,AN KAS Marius Jurgilas. Time to change the paradigm of cash I Bank of Lithuania MariusJurgilas.Time to changethe paradigmof cash 2017-09-14 MariusJurgilas,Memberof the Boardof the Bankof Lithuania.Articlein the EuroflMagazine/ Tallinn 2017 Despiteadvancesin financialdigitalizationthe most importantinstrumentin retailpaymentsstill is cash. As the 2015-2016 ECBcash usagesurveyshowed, three quartersof all paymentsat points-of-salein the euroarea are made in cash. Cash is king, as it is the only option for an ordinary person to hold onto the ultimate settlement asset central bank liabilities. Only the members of the gentlemen club of banks have direct access to the central bank reserve accounts. But this is changing. With this change we are changing the paradigm of cash . m1of 1 In the absence of trust we demand immediate settlement in something we trust more than the counterparty we are dealing with . Thus there is a structural demand for a central entity of trust to intermediate economic transactions. Money is that medium of exchange and cash is its ultimate-trust form. Commercial bank money is a near substitute of cash in most of the times and general public usually is ignorant of the notion of settlement finality or other legal discrepancies that make commercial bank money fundamentally different from central bank liabilities . But those differences become quite obvious and the ultimate-trust feature of cash and benefits of settlement in central bank liabilities becomes apparent during episodes of financial institution distress. And that is one of the reason why public prefers to hold onto the banknotes. Despite advances in financial digitalization the most important instrument in retail payments still is cash. 1/2 03/08/22, 14:36 MariusJurgilas.Time to changethe paradigmof cash I Bankof Lithuania Cash is what the public wants, thus it should be provided. But nobody said that cash must be tangible. The recent developments in technology make feasible broad provision and access to the central bank liabilities in electronic form. Cash can be digital. But that is no small development of the financial system. It would immediately reduce demand for commercial bank money. Such a change would have fundamental implications on credit growth, financial intermediation, transmission of monetary policy, and role of (central) banks in general. The foreseeable benefits of such a change in the paradigm of cash are tempting. No need for transaction balances at credit institutions, no need for deposit insurance, no more moral hazard, and maybe finally ... financial institutions that are not important enough to bail out. We should give it a try. Notes and coins. PaY.ments,Banks 2/2

It is my pleasure to have this opportunity to discuss with you the development of Baltic, Central and Eastern European capital markets in the context of Capital Markets Union. m1of 1 As we all know, the region is heavily dependent on traditional bank lending. This makes our financial systems vulnerable . It also limits the channels to finance the real economy, especially small and medium enterprises . Therefore, from the point of view of Baltic and Central and Eastern European states, Capital Markets Union development is of critical importance, as it helps, firstly, to create additional sources of funding and, secondly, to diversify risks. We must frankly admit that progress with Capital Markets Union development has not been as rapid as expected. This may suggest that a stronger national push is needed. However, we have to realize that placing too much emphasis on regional markets may lead to several competing regulatory blocks within the EU.That outcome should be avoided. Bearing this in mind, a possible way forward might be based on domestic best practices . Analyzing them and, when viable, transferring them to the EU level. Some countries,such as Lithuania,haveestablishedso-called'sandbox'regimesto gather the necessaryknowhow.Therefore,at this point,trying to construct effective EU-levelinstruments may be like walking blindfolded. On a broader note, I believethat novel solutions offer the possibility to strengthen capital markets in regions wherethey are currently underdeveloped.This would make the benefits of Capital Markets Union more evenlyspreadacross the EU. The Central Bank is responsible for the financial market development, thus we decided to roll out the red carpet for new entrants to inspire competition in the financial sector, where 90% of the market is controlled by three main Scandinavian banks : SEB, Swedbank and DNB. In their domestic markets, these banks were very innovative and at the forefront of providing ingenious consumer products. m1of 1 However, there were no competitive threats to the incumbents in Lithuania, so they did not have to invest in innovation and improvements here. We realized that the ultimate key to stimulating competition and challenge established norms lies in the collaboration with new market entrants and reducing market entry barriers for flntech companies. Moreover, we had to change the paradigm of a small market (Lithuania's population stands below 3 million). For this purpose, we adjusted the KYC regulation (similar to Germany) in order to allow remote identification of customers. Now flntech companies have access to 450 million consumers since they can remotely onboard them from all over Europe. If it is a startup, the ultimate goal for them is to get through the licensing process as fast as possible (within 3 months of submission of proper documents) and to start providing services and generating income (this can only happen if the application is done properly and if no impediments occur during the licensing process). This summerthe three largestmobileoperatorsin Lithuaniagot permissionfrom the European Commissionto createa commonplatformfor a mobilepaymentsservice.Couldyouelaboratea bit more on this projectand its benefitsfor consumersand merchants?
