Taiau prie tai  iandieninio pasaulio paveikslas, nes, kaip teisingai skelbia renginio antrat, ateit kuria dabartis. Globalioji ekonomika 2017 metais buvo geriausios bkls per vis deimtmet. Spariai augame ir iais metais. Matome, kad, nepaisant neramum ir neapibrtum, vidutiniu laikotarpiu augimas turt ilikti stabilus. Taiau dl atsirandani nauj prekybos apribojim pasaulio prekybos apimtis nominalia verte artimiausiu metu augs iek tiek liau. Be to, tarp region pasaulyje pradeda rykti pltros temp skirtumai. K tai pranaauja? Nenustebinsiu pasakydamas, kad pasaulinis galios balansas keiiasi. Negana to  gali bti, kad rykja naujos, arba tiksliau  jau kelis imtmeius nematytos daugiapols pasaulins tvarkos kontrai. 19 amius buvo Brit imperijos laikas. 20-asis  JAV takos apogjus. 21 amiuje JAV dominavimui ik meta Azija. Ikis drsus. Taiau lygiai taip pat  rimtas. Todl sulaukia labai vairi, netgi prietaring, taiau visuomet  labai rimt reakcij. Prisiminkime: Pivot to Asia  Atsigrimas  Azij. Tai buvo viena i pagrindini tuometinio JAV prezidento Baracko Obamos politikos linij, kuria signalizuoti du dalykai. Pirmasis  pripainimas, kad tarsi ant mielimusios augti ekonomikos yra labai perspektyvios. Antrasis  JAV nusiteikimas stiprinti ryius su jomis, tokiu bdu siekiant atsverti augani Kinijos tak regione. Dabartins JAV administracijos linija ir susijusi aplinka  kitokia... Dunda prekybos karo bgnai, sigalioja vis nauji JAV importo tarifai, iandien taikomi jau daugiau nei pusei Kinijos preki importo. Jei pridursime tai, kas iuo metu isakoma kaip ketinimai ar grasinimai, jau artimoje ateityje tarifai gali bti taikomi praktikai visoms  JAV i Kinijos veamoms prekms. Kinija, nors ir turdama maiau manevro laisvs (nes  JAV eksportuoja beveik 4 kartus daugiau preki, nei i jos importuoja), skolinga neliko  analogikus suvarymus ved didiajai daliai importo i JAV. Europos Sjungai iame myje pavyko ilikti nuoaliau ir net ssti su JAV atstovais prie deryb stalo. Tai jau is tas, net jei deryb baigtis kol kas neaiki,  tarkime, jei JAV gyvendint grasinimus papildomais tarifais apkrauti tokius ES strategikai svarbius sektorius kaip automobili pramon, atmosferos kaitimo galimyb ilikt itin reali. Apibendrinant tai, kas pasakyta: dviej JAV administracij reakcijos radikaliai skirtingos. Taiau bendra tarp j yra tai, kad abiem atvejais btent Kinija JAV usienio politikoje um itin svarbi viet. Ir prieastis abiem atvejais irgi greiiausiai  ta pati. J bent i dalies lemia ekonominiai procesai, ir i j kildinama prognoz, kad jau iemet Kinija pagal kio dyd turt aplenkti euro zon ir atsidurti antroje vietoje, ikart po JAV. Dalies ekspert vertinimu, didij ekonomini gali balansas keisis ir toliau. Jei j prognozs pasitvirtint, majant Europos ali svoriui pasaulinje ekonomikoje, 2032 m. Indija isivert treij viet, o Kinija  aplenkt JAV ir sitvirtint pirmoje pozicijoje. Didiausia Europos ekonomin galia  Vokietija  i ketvirtosios smuktelt penktj pozicij. Tiesa, primindamas, k jau kalbjau, i valg priskiriau diskutuotin kategorijai. Pirmiausia 32-ieji metai tebra toliau, nei siekia patikim prognozi horizontas. Antra  Kinija, kaip ir mes visi, susiduria su savais ikiais ir ieko bd juos atremti. Tuo pat metu sprendim savo klausimus tebeieko ir kitos alys, regionai, bendrijos. Todl iandien dar negalim inoti, nei kokie bus tie sprendimai, nei (kai kuriais atvejais) kas bus t sprendim primjai. Dl i prieasi  t. y. dl milijono neinomj  nedrsiau laintis, kas kuriais metais k aplenks. Taiau, vertindamas tai, kas akivaizdu, drsiau tvirtinti, kad kelis imtmeius stebt ryki mono- lyderyst turt pakeisti nauja  daugiapol ekonomikos tvarka. Tai reikia, kad negalime nepaisyti nauj ekonomins galios centr kilimo. Ir tikrai neturtume laukti nei 32-j, nei 22-j, nes jau ir iandien  2018-aisiais  turime pakankamai informacijos, kad galvotume, kokiais principais grsime partneryst su lyderiais Azijoje. Mums, europieiams, tai vis pirma reikia btinyb naujoje globalioje tvarkoje i naujo atrasti savo  t. y. Europos Sjungos  viet. Jei darome prielaid (o ji tikrai tiktina), kad JAV ir Kinijos galios varytuvs bei tampos ateityje dar stiprs, Europos Sjunga ia galt atlikti itin nauding atramins kolonos funkcij, neleidiani sutrkinti tiltui tarp Tolimj Ryt ir Vakar. Juk, viena vertus, su JAV mus sieja daugelio deimtmei transatlantin partneryst, ekonominiai, finansiniai ir saugumo saitai. Kita vertus, santykiuose su Kinija atrandame vis daugiau bendr tak. Pavyzdiui, Europos Sjunga jau iandien bendradarbiauja su Kinija ties Pasaulins prekybos organizacijos reformos iniciatyva. Btent Europos Sjungos tarpininkavimo dka Kinija prisijung prie Paryiaus klimato kaitos susitarimo ir iliko jo dalimi net kai i susitarimo nusprend pasitraukti JAV. Toki bendrysts pavyzdi yra ir daugiau. Aplinkybsities palankios  Europos Sjunga atsidr unikalioje pozicijoje, kai gali atlikti skmingo ir takingo mediatoriaus vaidmen. Kas mums i to ir kaip t pasiekti? Kolegos, tektonini poslinki kontekste privalome blaiviai vertinti savo viet ir gali pasaulyje. Prieimt met Europoje gyveno ketvirtadalis pasaulio gyventoj. iandien tik kas deimtas ems mogus yra europietis, ir i dalis  maja. Deja, i aplinkyb nesukuria pagrindo tiktis, kad ateinaniais deimtmeiais msemyno ekonomin, politin ir kultrintaka savaime stiprs. Greiiau atvirkiai. Todl privalome rasti nauj bd isaugoti viet prie takingj deryb stalo. Ir vis pirma  usitikrinti, kad atramin kolona, galbt galinti paremti trkinjant JAVKinijos tilt, nesutrupt pati. Esu i t, kurie tiki, kad btent gilesn integracija yra atsakas  neigiamas tendencijas: fragmentacij ir stiprjant populizm. Savo ruotu, esmin gilesns integracijos dedamoji  tai efektyvesn ekonomin valdysena. Todl bent man vili teikia tai, kad pastaruoju metu diskusijos dlbtinybs stiprinti ekonomins ir pinig sjungos pamatus tapo ir aktyvesns, ir intensyvesns. Tiktina, kad jas kursto ir artjanti kadencijos pabaiga  tiek Europos palamento, tiek ir Komisijos. Taiau net tokiu atveju tai, kad jau gruod tikimasi sprendim dl Europos stabilumo mechanizmo pertvarkos, yra labai gera inia. Detalmis nekankinsiu, tik pasakysiu, kad ios reformos esm  sudaryti slygas alims, vos pastebjus kylanias finansinio stabilumo rizikas, gauti prevencins paramos paket  savotik kreditin kortel. Kortelsl panaudoti nebtina  vien jos turjimo faktas gali nuraminti investuotoj nuogstavimus dl alies mokumo. O tai reikia  ukardyti galim krizs siliepsnojim ir sustiprinti ne tik tos alies, bet ir euro zonos finansin stabilum. Dar viena labai svarbi detal: tokia kreditin kortelbt prieinama tik paangioms narms, besilaikanioms taisykli ir savo vieuosius finansus tvarkanioms drausmingai. Panau, kad gruod taip pat turt bti patvirtintas papildomas Europos Sjungos Bendro pertvarkymo fondo finansavimas. Tai leis bti tikresniems, jog gelbstint lunganius bankus neprireiks valstybi biudet, o tai yra  mokesi moktoj pinig. Europos indli garantij sistemos perspektyva. Jeigu iose diskusijose proveris pagaliau vyks, tai bt didiulis pasiekimas stiprinant ekonomin ir pinig sjung. Europinis indli draudimas suvienodint indlinink apsaug visoje Bendrijoje  kiekvieno taupaniojo l apsauga bt garantuojama visos Europos bank sektoriaus. Toks mechanizmas sudaryt slygas kurtis efektyvesniems, masto ekonomij inaudojantiems tarptautiniams bankams bei sustiprint pasitikjim Bendrijos finans sektoriaus stabilumu. Tai taip pat bt tiek pasauliui, tiek europieiams reikalinga inia, kad Bendrija sugeba ne tik generuoti idjas, bet ir jas realizuoti, arba, kitaip tariant,  ubaigti, k pradjusi. iuo konkreiu atveju tai btgyvendintas bank sjungos projektas. Galiausiai  euro zonos biudetas. Ant stalo  vairios idjos ir projektai, kuriuos teik tiek ES institucijos, tiek ir ali vyriausybs. Umojai skirtingi  nuo 0,3 proc. BVP, kurie, perskaiiavus  eurus, reikt apie 30 milijard, iki net keleto BVP procent, kurie reiktimtus milijard. Nemanau, kad iandien turime galimyb detaliau aptarti ias idjas. Taiau miniu jas kaip rodym, kad Europa, pirma, pripasta didesnio solidarumo poreik. Antra  suvokia gilesns integracijos btinyb. Ir treia  nra praradusi ambicij isaugoti ir galbt plsti tarptautin ekonomintak. Pavyzdiui, gilesn ekonomin integracija ir platesnio masto rizik padalijimas tarp valstybi nari leist padidinti euro kaip rezervins valiutos naudojim. Nors euras tebra antra svarbiausia pasaulin rezervin valiuta, atotrkis nuo JAV dolerio ilieka didiulis. Negana to, usienio valiutos atsarg eurais dalis pasaulyje sumajo nuo 24 proc. 2005 m. iki 20 proc. pernai. Nordami sumainti atsilikim nuo JAV dolerio, sudaranio daugiau nei 60 proc. vis usienio valiutos atsarg, privalome stiprinti tarptautin euro vaidmen. Ar tai pavyks? K tik minjau kelet pozityvienkl. Taiau  net ir j fone  neapleidia jausmas, kad gilesns ekonomins integracijos perspektyvos gali nutolti. Galimybi langas svarbesnms pertvarkoms gali susiaurti jau po 2019 m. gegusmn. Europos Parlamento rinkim. Kita vertus, matant, kad alys nars nesilaiko iandienini sipareigojim, sunku tiktis, jog pavyks pasiekti reikming prover tariantis dl rizik pasidalijimo ir didesnio finansinio solidarumo ateityje. tai rodymas. Europos Komisija valstybms narms teikia rekomendacijas, pagrstas j pai bendrai sutartomis taisyklmis. Matome lidn paveiksl, parodant, jog gyvendinam rekomendacij skaiius kasmet maja. 2012 m. reikminga paanga fiksuota gyvendinant 11 proc. rekomendacij. 2016 m. i 86-i rekomendacij reikmingiau pasistmta gyvendinant tik dvi. Pernai progresas pasiektas gyvendinant vos vien rekomendacij (i 76). Dar lidnesnis pastarj savaii pavyzdys. Jau minjau  vyksta lemiamos derybos dl svarbiausi reform, kurios gali sustiprinti  arba ne  ekonomin ir pinig sjung. Ir tuo pat metu girdime apie itin iurktaus sutart fiskalini taisykli nepaisymo atvej. is atvejis ypatingas dar ir tuo, kad reikming valdios ilaid didinim numatanti vyriausyb atvirai pripasta suprantanti, kad jos biudetas paeis fiskalins drausms reikalavimus. Kitaip tariant, susitarimas lauomas smoningai. Toks atviras konfrontacinis tonas, neturintis precedento Stabilumo ir augimo pakto istorijoje, tikrai nestiprina ekonomins integracijos idjos. O be jos skmingai aisti aukiausioje lygoje bt sunku. Gerbiamieji, ors paveikslas jau dabar atrodo sudtingas, rizikuosiu j sukomplikuoti dar labiau. Nes kartu su globaliaisiais gali poslinkiais ir europiniais vidaus procesais vyksta ir kiti  ne maiau doms pokyiai, kuriuos iuo atveju gal teisingiau bt vadinti virsmais. Kalbame apie ateit, tad, jei nenorime bti jos uklupti nepasiruo,j ignoruoti negalime. Jau per artimiausius deimt met pajusime, k atnea 4-oji pramons revoliucija, i esms pertvarkanti ekonomikos struktr bei atskir jos sektori veikimo principus. Natralu, kad i kaita neaplenkia ir finans sektoriaus. Finansini technologij  arba FinTech  banga yra iliustratyvus to pavyzdys: dirbtinio intelekto, blok grandins, didij duomen (big data) sprendimai jau dabar keiia finans sektoriaus veid. Ir aiku, kad keis dar esmingiau. Pirmoje i met pusje pasaulins investicijos  FinTech bendroves siek beveik 60 mlrd. JAV doleri. Tai reikia, kad vien per pirmji met pusmet investicij bta 1/3 daugiau nei per visus 2017 metus ir 3/4 daugiau nei prie 5 metus. I to daryiau ivad, kad investuotojai mato inovacij finans sektoriuje perspektyv. Ir kad investicijos i srit jau siekia t mast, kuris turi potencialo ilgainiui pakeisti finans sektori. Mes tikims, kad  gera. Pirmiausia  kad inovatyvs finansini technologij sprendimai finans sektoriuje paskatins konkurencij. i valg pagrsiu mums artimiausiu  Lietuvos mokjim rinkos pavyzdiu. Susijungus dviem bankams didiosios trijuls dalis ms mokjim rinkoje uima apie 80 proc. Ms vertinimas vienareikmis: tokia koncentracija  negerai. Taiau gerai yra tai,  rink ateina nauji alternatyvs  t. y. nebankiniai  mokjimo paslaug teikjai. J atjim skatiname, ir jau iuo metu LT finans rinkoje turime apie 115 Fintech moni. Vien elektronini pinigstaig skaiius tik per pastaruosius pusantr met iaugo daugiau nei 5 kartus. Akivaizdu, kad ledas pajudjo. Koks rezultatas? Ne bank teikiama elektronini mokjim dalis iuo metu jau virija deimtadal, o tendencijos rodo, kad i dalis didja su pagreiiu. Ir, tiktina, dids iuo metu vertiname dar apie 40 nauj paraik gauti FinTech licencijas. Kitaip tariant, FinTech meta pirtin tradicinms finansstaigoms. ios, kad isaugot pozicijas, privals paisyti nauj realij ir besikeiiani kliento poreiki. Privals keisti savo verslo modelius, ideologijas ir elgsenas. Ties sakant  jau keiia. Pavyzdiui, du bankai, dar visai neseniai buv itin skeptiki, pradeda teikti momentini mokjim paslaug. Tai reikia, kad FinTech pirtin  pakelta. Kitas lkestis, kuris siejamas su FinTech, tai finans sistemos demokratizavimas. Pasaulio banko vertinimu, 1,7 mlrd. moni (daugiau nei penktadalis ems gyventoj) vis dar neturi prieigos prie elementari finansini paslaug  tarkime, negali atsidaryti sskaitos banke. FinTech sprendimai yra tai, kas gali keisti ir keiia toki padt i esms. kart pagrindimui  tolesnis, taiau ypatikinamas pavyzdys  Usachario Afrika. Beveik pus pasaulins mobilij atsiskaitym rinkos tenka btent iam regionui. Aktyviai naudojam mobilij piniginiia 70 (septyni ir nulis) kart daugiau nei Europoje ir Centrinje Azijoje kartu sudjus. Afrika yra pasaulin lyder mobilij mokjim srityje, ir btent tai leido reikmingai padidinti emyno gyventoj, kurie m aktyviai naudotis finansinmis paslaugomis, skaii. Finansins technologijos Afrikai suteik unikali galimyb perokti tradicins bankininkysts etap ir nuo grynj pereiti tiesiai prie elektronini alternatyv. Tikiuosi, kad ios technologijos pakeis ir kit visuomeni santykius su grynaisiais, kurie toms visuomenms kainuoja tikrai nemaai. Taip pat tikiuosi, tiksliau  neabejoju, kad Fintech priemons gali reikmingai iplsti kreditavimo altini rat. Skaiiuojama, kad pasaulinis tarpusavio (peer-to-peer) skolinomo mastas, augantis madaug 50 % kasmet, 2024 metais turt pasiekti 900 mlrd. JAV doleri. spdingas skaiius, galintis palankiai paveikti ir kredito prieinamum, ir kainas, ir kreditavimo tradicijas plaija prasme. Kolegos, spju, kad apie privalumus pakaks  esate tikrai ne ta auditorija, kurioje reikt pasakoti apie inovacij teikiamas galimybes. Neabejoju, kad girdjote ir apie rizikas. Taiau jas priminti privalau, nes nauji finansiniai produktai, nauji j pateikimo kanalai, nauji IT sprendimai, reikalaujantys duomen atvrimo ir skaitmenini ssaj su banko sskaita, reikia naujus ikius tiek paslaug teikjams, tiek ir j gavjams. Kaip juos veikti? Ne atsitverti, bet atsiverti naujovms. Prisijaukinti ir darbinti savo ir visuomens naudai. Mes Lietuvos banke vadovaujamsbtent iuo principu, ir, drstu pasidiaugti,  jis veikia. Kalbant konkreiau, prie kelet met isiklme sau tiksl, kad Lietuvos bankas dirbs ne tik kaip prievaizdas,  kas neivengiamai yra ms priederms dalis,  bet ir kaip finans sektoriaus partneris. Konsultuojame ir patariame pradedantiems veikl. Neseniai rengme smlio d,  t. y. sukrme slygas konstruoti ir ibandyti inovatyvius verslo modelius, kartu suteikiant sau galimyb atnaujinti reguliaciniranki arsenal. diegme imanij elektroninio licencijavimo priemon, kuri potencialiems rinkos dalyviams leidia paraik dl licencijos pateikti nuotoliniu bdu. Dl ko taip stengiams? Jau minjau, kad esame U inovacijas, kurios gali suteikti finans ateiiai mums palanki krypt. Kita vertus,  kad turtume galimyb t krypt koreguoti norima linkme, privalome engti ne i paskos ir ne koja kojon su rinkos pokyiais, o ma maiausiai puse ingsnio priekyje. Tai  btina slyga suvaldyti jau mintus ir taip pat nepamintus ikius  tokius kaip kibernetinis saugumas, tarptautinio pinig plovimo grsm, arba ilgesniuoju laikotarpiu galimai ikilsianias rizikas, susijusias su finans sistemos fragmentacija bei ikiais finansiniam stabilumui  ypa jei ir toliau fiksuosime spartvairi kriptoturto kategorij augim. Grtant prie globalaus paveikslo: minjau, kad Europos Sjunga turi ans (jei sugebs juo pasinaudoti) uimti moderuojanios atramos tarp JAV ir Kinijos vaidmen. Kiekviena Bendrijos naria gali atrasti savo ni ir neti savo indl. Prisipainsiu, taip nemaai apie Fintech kalbjau neatsitiktinai. Mes Lietuvos banke tikime, kad Lietuvos nia gali bti btent tilt tiesimas FinTech sektoriuje. ioje srityje jau turime dirb. Aktyviai mezgame ryius su Azijos alimis, pleiame tarpinstitucinio bendradarbiavimo geografij: Lietuvos finansmonms yra atvertas kelias tiesiogiai investuoti  Kinijos kapitalo rink. Esame pasira bendradarbiavimo susitarim su Kinijos bank reguliavimo institucija. iemet pasirame susitarim dl bendradarbiavimo FinTech klausimais su Singapro centriniu banku. Taip pat mms koordinatoriaus vaidmens vystant bendr Kinijos bei Vidurio ir Ryt Europos ali veikl pltojant finansinms technologijoms palanki aplink. iame ir kituose formatuose Lietuv Azijos alims pristatome kaip vartus  Europos bank ir mokjimo rink. Tokiam prisistatymui turime prieasi.Ms taikomas FinTech moni licencijavimo reimas yra ne tik vienas spariausi Europoje, bet ir vienas lanksiausi, silantis plat veiklos modeli pasirinkim. Be to, elektronini pinig ir mokjimo staigoms esame atvr centrinio banko mokjim infrastruktr  per ms CENTROlink platform FinTech mons gali tiesiogiai, be joki tarpinink, pasiekti vis SEPA erdv. Matome, kad tokios prieigos perspektyva domi treijalimonms, siekianioms engti  Europos rink. Ja domisi ir Kinijos verslas. Veiklos licencijas jau esame suteik penkioms ios alies FinTech monms. Dar trys yra pateikusios praymus ir iuo metu yra vertinamos. Kontakt srautas rodo, kad interesas neslgsta. inoma, finansins technologijos nra vienintel nia, kuri gali uimti Lietuva, iekodama vietos naujoje pasaulio tvarkoje. Vis dlto btent ia a matau labai apiuopiam, pasiekiam ir potencialo nestokojani galimyb. Kadangi iandien ne kart minjau Azij ir Kinij, prisiminiau sen t krat posak: galimyb duris beldiasi tik kart. J labai graiai papildo europiei patarl: jei galimyb nesibeldia  sistatyk duris. Taigi  kalbdami, svajodami, prognozuodami ir kurdami ateit bkime budrs. Kai beldia  atidarykime. O kai neatidaro  drskime pasibelsti... Dkoju u dmes. Lietuvos banko valdybos pirmininko pristatymas (1.9 MB download icon)

Title: Interview to the daily "Verslo inios"
text: Interview of Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, to the daily "Verslo zinios", 30/04/2019 Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, is interviewed by Dalius Simnas. The interview was published on 30 April 2019 in the daily "Verslo zinios". What trends do you see in the banking sector, what do you predict for the future? I would say that, in general, we have been witnessing steady growth in the economy and the banking sector since 2015, and 2018 was really good for banks in terms of returns, the coincidence with the economic cycle is direct. Last year, economic development reached its peak, this year, according to our assessment, we are growing above potential, although we are forecasting slightly slower growth. The banking sector is moving in a similar way, both in terms of lending and income earned. For some time now, debt to suppliers has been growing faster than debts to banks, and in many sectors this year, delays in settlement have also been observed. How do you see that? Debt growth in the boom period is a natural phenomenon. The increased obligations of companies to suppliers can be explained by the fact that in reality only a few banks lend, when one market participant (luminor bank's branch in Lithuania  Vz) is currently reorganizing, his attention to the main activity is weakened, so I believe that in the medium term, when the bank will start operating as a single organism in all the Baltic States, then, apparently, we will be able to expect faster lending. In the case of debts to suppliers, we are talking about a chain that is more sensitive and can affect many non-financial enterprises in that chain, so the likelihood of a chain reaction during a market fall is higher than when working with professional credit institutions that know how to deal with customers during economic ups and downs. Within a few years, the status of the secondary bank was changed by several market participants. How do you evaluate the process of branching banks? What are its disadvantages, dangers? Structural changes are associated with the search for efficiency. Naturally, banking groups weigh, do a cost-benefit analysis and make decisions that allow you to make operations more efficient. A classic supervisor would say that the branching of banks is very bad, because the supervision of secondary banks comes out of our hands. They turn into branches, which become the object of supervision of the already original bank. I look at this in a simpler way, because we live in a time of banking union, when co-European regulation is becoming more universal and cooperation between supervisors is intensifying. Of course, the branching of banks touches on the issue of deposit insurance. For example, in the case of Luminor, the deposit insurance risk, whatever it may be, in this case moved to Estonia. Therefore, in order for the secondary bank and branch supervision to be the same, we need to complete the Banking Union by putting the third leg of this union, the European deposit insurance. As I understand it, the decisions on this day are frozen? At least until the election of the new European Commission (in November this year, the Vz), it would hardly be possible to agree on a final deposit insurance scheme. Title: Crediting and financial services in Lithuania
text: Crediting and financial services in Lithuania Speech by Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, during the conference of the Seimas Committee on Budget and Finance and the Bank of Lithuania "How we will replace outgoing banks in the regions: problems, opportunities and prospects". Vilnius, 20 November 2019 The text is not a transcript of the language Good afternoon, the honored guests of the event, dear colleagues, we gathered today, because the current trends in the availability of financial services in one way or another are troubling part of our society. It is clear that the picture of the financial services market is changing. At this point, I propose two things: firstly, to talk about the facts that is, to clearly identify the areas where we are actually facing real problems; secondly, to be constructive, that is, to see both the problems and the solutions that are already being implemented, while also anticipating possible next steps. Therefore, today, based on the facts, I will try to summarize the current trends in the availability of credit and financial services. Next, I will discuss the regulatory changes that are being made or are needed in order to achieve greater access to financial services. Crediting and financial services in Lithuania So  crediting. Indeed, bank lending has been somewhat muted lately. According to the latest data, while the portfolio of bank loans granted to businesses and households is still growing, growth has slowed down. It is true that two different trends need to be highlighted here: lending by credit institutions to households  we are seeing a green arrow  is still fast. It stands at 8% and far exceeds the growth rate of the country's economy. And lending to companies has noticeably muted. I'll start with the household. In recent years, wages have risen at an extremely fast pace, consumer expectations  too. These factors have encouraged residents to buy real estate, so the bank's housing loan portfolio has also grown significantly - by almost about 10 percent. Growth has not been slowed down even by the recent rise in interest rates. Credit and financial services in Lithuania The rapid growth rate of housing loans has already become a common message, so without staying on it longer, I would like to draw attention to another  new  phenomenon: the growth of housing loans is currently strongly expressed not only in the largest cities of the country, but in principle in all regions. Even in the most passive in this sense, in Utena county, housing loans increased by almost 3 percent in the most active counties  Vilnius, Kaunas and siauliai  counties, in the third quarter of this year, the annual growth of the housing loan portfolio fluctuated around 9 percent. Consumer loans. The portfolio of bank loans for purposes other than buying housing is also increasing, but the pace is probably half as slow as the development of housing loans. However  again, I will pay attention a new thing  we note that recently consumer loans are increasingly being granted by non-banks, and other consumer credit lenders. Looking at the annual changes, the consumer credit portfolio of banks shrank by 3 percent. However, the portfolio of other consumer credit lenders (e.g. leasing providers) grew by almost a quarter. So it is obvious: alternatives are developing in the consumer credit segment, and we are already seeing the real result of these processes. This is good news for consumers. Crediting and financial services in LithuaniaThe mood in the enterprise credit market is slightly different. We have seen that bank lending to companies has been muted, and according to the latest data, over the year even decreased by 1 per cent. Surveys conducted by the Bank of Lithuania at the beginning of 2018 and 2019 showed another significant change  a significant increase in the number of cases when business applications for credit are rejected. For example, in 2017, banks refused to comply with 16% of business applications, and this year the proportion of rejected applications doubled to 30%. In the category of smallcompanies, this proportion is even larger. The decrease in lending by credit institutions is recorded in most sectors of the economy, but we can single out the largest group of borrowers  real estate developers. Lending to these companies in recent years has contributed the most to the overall growth of the business loan portfolio, but at the moment the portfolio of loans to real estate companies is not only no longer growing, but even decreasing. The portfolio is also shrinking in other sectors: production, construction, agriculture. There's perhaps one glaring exception [not counting the sporadic loans to holding companies that popped up from time to time]  the transport sector, to which lending to which lending has increased markedly in recent years. This was due to the rapid development of the transport sector in Lithuania, which was characterized by investments in the vehicle fleet. I'll remind you  every tenth worker in the country currently works in the transport sector. With these trends  I mean declining lending to businesses  there are two questions that arise. The first is that what is causing the decline in lending to companies? The second is that companies have alternatives? Answering the first question, it is important to assess structural changes in the market for lenders. Here we can see that the lending of some banks has continued to increase, while that of others has been noticeably shrinking. And here a significant role was played by the decrease in the loan portfolio of one bank, probably also related to the affairs of the restructuring of that bank. Indeed, the concentration of the Lithuanian banking sector is particularly high  too high  so one bank can strongly influence the trends of the entire market. Other reasons may have contributed to the mutation of crediting. For example, some banks most likely began to feel the "saturation" of loans granted to some sectors. On the other hand, the companies that participated in the survey of the Bank of Lithuania acknowledged that loan applications are usually rejected due to their poorly assessed financial situation or the general context of the economic situation. This may mean that banks have also become more risk-sensitive. Let us move on to the second question: how are things going with alternatives to financing companies? Credit and financial services in Lithuania Data shows that, despite the fact that companies borrowed less frequently from banks, the share of their obligations in their total wealth has increased over several years! Or to be more precise  it has increased significantly  from 38 to 45 per cent. From the picture we see obvious evidence, which means, first of all, that there are alternative countries and that companies are able to find and use them. What are these sources? I would single out some of the most significant ones. First, companies are increasingly inclined to borrow from other non-financial firms. Both companies' short-term indebtedness to suppliers is increasing  let's call them trade credits, as well as long-term loans from other companies. According to statistics, corporate trade credits increased by almost EUR 1 billion over the year, while the portfolio of long-term loans from other enterprises grew by almost EUR 270 million. The popularity of such borrowing is enhanced by the fact that as the economy grows, the financial situation of companies is strong and a significant part of them has the opportunity to lend. In addition, for several years in a row, borrowing from financial institutions other than banks, including leasing companies, has been growing rapidly. In a year, long-term debts to non-bank financial institutions grew by EUR 260 million. Eur. Other alternative sources of financing are also gaining popularity, such as bond borrowing. Although bonds are still rarely issued, last year we had a number of particularly large issues that totaled over EUR 660 million. Thus, this market is also being discovered more and more often. Borrowing through crowdfunding platforms and funds is also rapidly increasing. Let's say that during these years, companies borrowed over 23 million on such platforms. Recent trends make it possible to hope that this type of borrowing will continue to gain popularity. The results of the Bank of Lithuania's surveys also confirm the growing willingness of companies to finance with alternative sources. For example, about a third of companies engaged in manufacturing and construction activities say that they feel the need for alternative sources of financing. There is a growing number of companies that not only recognize the need, but also say that they have real plans to change the sources of financing in the near future. Over the last three years, the share of such enterprises has more than doubled, from 7% to 15%. In general, it is worth noting that the share of bank loans tends to decrease in corporate commitments, while the share of other commitments tends to increase. It is therefore important to ensure that the availability of alternative sources is sufficient. About how we strive for this and how we encourage it, a little later. Thus, summing up the above, we see that housing lending is growing in all regions of Lithuania, companies borrow less from banks and more often use alternative methods of financing. And what do we see in another, especially important, segment of financial services  payments? Crediting and financial services in Lithuania Indeed, in the area of payments, the situation is changing very quickly. There are a lot of changes, but the key feature is one  Payment services all over the world, including in Lithuania, are moving to the digital space. We will not stop this and we will not turn back. Therefore, we have to state the undeniable fact that the number of physical customer service departments in Lithuania is decreasing, some of them do not perform operations with cash. The atm network is also optimizing and, to put it more simply, it is also thinning. From 2015 to the present, the number of customer service points of physical banks in Lithuania has decreased by several dozen. Bank branches providing cash services have more than halved. However, in Lithuania, cash still occupies a very important part of the market  almost 20% of the population receives wages or other income in cash, i.e. every fifth resident. By the way, in this sense, the habits of the inhabitants of metropolitan areas and other cities and villages are different - it is the latter who prefer cash more often. So what alternatives remain for residents of the regions as the network of bank branches and ATMs becomes thinning? As banks in Lithuania focus their services on the electronic space, other  non-bank  market participants take over part of the cash payments market. Statistics show that as many as 90% of transfers initiated at physical customer service points in 2018 were made not in banks, but in payment and electronic money offices, such as post office, "Perlas" terminals, cash desks of shopping centers or newsstands. These market participants are attractive to the population because, firstly, they have a much wider network for the provision of such services and, secondly, they apply more favorable pricing of cash transactions. Residents of rural and smaller cities are more actively using the non-banking network to withdraw cash from the account or pay for utilities. I would like to draw attention to credit unions. We can see that in the regions they are becoming able to provide a partial counterweight to the outgoing bank branches. In III quarter 2019, credit unions had 160 customer service branches (I will remind you  there were 250 bank branches). Credit and financial services in Lithuania Are gradually changing the habits of the residents themselves. The number of non-cash payments made in Lithuania is increasing at an increasingly significant pace  last year the growth amounted to 14 per cent. But, even with such growth, we still do not reach the European average. Let's compare: in Lithuania, there are only over 200 non-cash payment transactions per capita, and on average in the euro area this figure is approaching 270. On the other hand, we can expect the popularity of non-cash payments to continue to increase. The prerequisites for this are created: 88 percent. Lithuanian residents have at least one payment account, 84 per cent  a payment card. Those with an account are increasingly making orders online. Moreover, as many as 4 out of 5 residents say that instant payments are a necessary and attractive payment service for them. Instant payment infrastructure, process automation, open banking and other innovations currently being applied particularly rapidly in the payments market have their own advantages. First of all, they increase the simplicity and convenience of payments for the population  be it contactless payment cards that have already become commonplace or instant payments that are rapidly spreading. Secondly, the digitalisation of payment services makes payments cheaper for both businesses and residents, partly because there is more competition in the electronic payments market. So, digitalisation is essentially an unavoidable future for payments. The trouble is that part of the population does not keep up with the changes, such as seniors or those living in more remote rural areas. Therefore, the transition to new, more efficient payments cannot take place without a sigh of relief  without taking into account sensitive groups in society. It is important to look for ways to ensure adequate access to traditional means for sensitive groups of society, as well as to seriously engage in the education of the population. Residents of the regions usually have tools for non-cash payments, but they cannot always pay with them. For this reason, it is important to make it possible to pay comfortably everywhere, even in small business enterprises. For this, business owners need options that are attractive to them for accepting payments. At the stage of change, dialogue between small businesses, banks and other payment service providers and users is important. A discussion is needed as to what level of service is acceptable and would serve the interests of citizens and businesses, as well as payment service providers, and how the costs would be covered. Particular attention must be paid to the financial education of the younger generation. As a result, the Payments Council, established on the initiative of the Bank of Lithuania, has set up a task group uniting representatives of payment service providers and users, which is looking for ways to strengthen youth payment skills. Consumers need to understand the services they use, know their benefits and know how to use them safely. Such knowledge will be an inevitable part of everyday life in the future. In addition to the establishment of the already mentioned Payments Council, I would like to highlight the regulatory changes that have already increased or, in my opinion, have great potential to further increase the availability of financial services in Lithuania. Credit and financial services in Lithuania One of the success stories I would consider the reform of the credit union sector, which I have already mentioned, for which we laid the foundations back in 2016. Thanks to the joint efforts of the country's institutions, it was possible to successfully restructure the sector, which finally emerged from the long-standing deep problems and became indisputably "healthier". During the restructuring, firstly, the capital regulation of credit unions was tightened; secondly, their compulsory membership in central credit unions has been established, thus ensuring the integration of the entire sector, and thirdly, the mechanisms for mutual assistance of the system of central credit unions are clearly defined. Now we are already seeing the fruit. The credit union sector is no longer becoming a potential, but a truly real alternative to credit in the regions. The annual growth rate of the loan portfolio of the loans they have granted is currently close to 20%, and the sector itself is operating profitably and stably. That's what we were aiming for when we started the transformation. That is what we expect from this sector in the future. Another initiative is the active invitation of new financial market participants, including banks, to carry out their activities in Lithuania. Back in 2016, the Bank of Lithuania approved its strategy of attracting new market participants. We have established a specialized bank license, are actively implementing the Newcomer program for potential newcomers to the market, we have established a regulatory sandbox  a friendly space for startups creating financial innovations. We are already seeing the first results of these efforts. Since the end of 2018, the European Central Bank has already granted four new ones with the Bank of Lithuania banking licenses, and four more applications for licenses are currently under consideration. Thus, we can also expect a further increase in alternatives in the country's banking sector. The new banks (Revolut Bank UAB, European Merchant Bank UAB, AB "Mano bankas" and UAB General Financing) will specialize either in consumer lending or intend to fill a relevant niche in small and medium-sized business lending. These banks will also collect deposits from retail clients, and some will also offer payment services. Some of the new banks are already providing services to customers, while others are in a phase of intensive preparation. Although today it is still difficult to quantify the benefits of new banks, we can already see the coming capital, the creation of new jobs and the emergence of more modern services for customers. I stress: we carry out the licensing process for new banks in accordance with the highest standards of supervision new banks are subject to the same assessment criteria as any other bank in the euro area. The licence shall in all cases be issued by the ECB. Of course, the supervision we are implementing is also in line with the standards for banking supervision in the euro area. In recent years, the Bank of Lithuania has also contributed to other regulatory changes that have strengthened the financial services market. Here again, I would recall the already mentioned popular forms of alternative financing: peer-to-peer lending, crowdfunding and collective investment undertakings. We regulated peer-to-peer lending, i.e. people's lending to people (person to person) through peer-to-peer lending platforms, back in 2016. Although it is still a relatively young sector, we currently have six platforms with the right to provide consumer credit and two with housing credit. We can be pleased that the number of both borrowers and investors is growing noticeably. According to the data of the end of June of this year, the number of borrowers amounted to 15.8 thousand, and the number of those wishing to lend was even higher  27.2 thousand. In 2016, the crowdfunding institute was also regulated, which provides an opportunity to attract the funds necessary for business development from the public. Lithuania is one of the first Member States of the European Union to create a legal regulatory environment for crowdfunding. Currently, twelve crowdfunding platform operators have the right to provide services in Lithuania. We see that the platforms finance real estate projects, small business projects, refinance business loans and attract working capital. Since 2016, the crowdfunding market has only grown. Over the entire period of existence of crowdfunding platforms, funds were collected in this way for 471 projects. Finally, in order to expand business opportunities to use alternative sources of financing, the Bank of Lithuania has focused on improving the regulatory environment of collective investment undertakings or, more simply, investment funds, over the past two years. Such funds invest the accumulated funds in the shares or bonds of enterprises, thereby providing the business with the necessary capital. However, in 2019 February. amendments to the legislation came into force, which enabled mutual funds to invest directly in loans to businesses. In the first half of 2019, there were 102 collective investment undertakings operating in Lithuania with a total net asset value of almost EUR 1 billion. Eur. Colleagues, together, including the contribution of the Seimas and the Government, we have implemented many important changes. The effort has paid off  there are positive changes. I believe that this encourages and encourages us not to stop and to make financial services more beneficial to society and to increase their availability. In view of the recent increase in concentration in the banking sector, we need to encourage the development of alternatives to credit and other financial services. This requires creating a favourable investment environment and acting in a targeted way  by coordinating actions between institutions and seeing a common goal. How are we going to do what? I hope that today's meeting will be able to share, not only observations, insights and reproaches, but also constructive proposals, the implementation of which will provide us with better financial services for everyone across the country. Pabriu: nauj bank licencijavimo proces vykdome vadovaudamiesi aukiausiais prieiros standartais  naujiems bankams taikomi tokie pat vertinimo kriterijai, kaip ir steigiant bet kur kit euro zonos bank. Licencij visais atvejais iduoda ECB. Be abejons, ms gyvendinama prieira taip pat atitinka euro zonos bank prieirai keliamus standartus. Pastaraisiais metais Lietuvos bankas prisidjo ir prie kit reguliavimo pokyi, sustiprinusi finansini paslaug rink. Ir ia vl priminiau jau mintas populiarjanias alternatyvaus finansavimo formas: tarpusavio skolinim, sutelktin finansavim ir kolektyvinius investavimo subjektus. Tarpusavio skolinim, t. y. moni skolinimmonms (angl. person to person) per tarpusavio skolinimo platformas, reglamentavome dar 2016 m. Nors tai vis dar pakankamai jaunas sektorius, iuo metu turime eias platformas, turinias teis teikti vartojimo kreditus, ir dvi  bsto kreditus. Galime pasidiaugti, kad pastebimai auga tiek besiskolinanij, tiek ir investuojanij skaiius. i met birelio pabaigos duomenimis, besiskolinanij skaiius sudar 15,8 tkst., o norinij paskolinti buvo dar daugiau  27,2 tkst. 2016 m. reglamentuotas ir sutelktinio finansavimo institutas, suteikiantis galimyb verslo pltrai reikalingas las prisitraukti i visuomens. Lietuva yra viena pirmj Europos Sjungos valstybi nari, sukrusi teisin reguliacin aplink sutelktiniam finansavimui. iuo metu teis teikti paslaugas Lietuvoje turi dvylika sutelktinio finansavimo platform operatori. Matome, kad platformose finansuojami nekilnojamojo turto projektai, smulkiojo verslo projektai, refinansuojamos verslo paskolos ir pritraukiamos apyvartinslos. Nuo 2016 m. sutelktinio finansavimo rinka tik augo. Per vis sutelktinio finansavimo platform gyvavimo laikotarp tokiu bdu los buvo renkamos 471 projektui. Galiausiai, Lietuvos bankas, siekdamas plsti verslo galimybes naudoti alternatyvius finansavimo altinius, pastaruosius dvejus metus daug dmesio skyr kolektyvinio investavimo subjekt arba paprasiau  investicini fond reguliacins aplinkos tobulinimui. Tokie fondai sukauptas las investuoja moni akcijas ar obligacijas, taip suteikdami verslui reikiamo kapitalo. Taiau 2019 m. vasario mn. sigaliojo teiss akt pakeitimai, galin investicinius fondus investuoti tiesiogiai  paskolas verslui. 2019 m. pirmj pusmet Lietuvoje veik 102 kolektyvinio investavimo subjektai, kuri bendra grynj aktyv vert yra beveik 1 mlrd. Eur. Kolegos, kartu, skaitant Seimo ir Vyriausybs indl, gyvendinome daug svarbi pokyi. Pastangos pasiteisino  teigiam pokyi yra. Manau, jog tai drsina ir skatina nesustoti ir siekti, kad finansins paslaugos kurt didesn naud visuomenei, o j prieinamumas didt. Matydami pastarojo meto koncentracijos bank sektoriuje didjim, turime paskatinti kreditavimo ir kit finansini paslaug teikimo alternatyv krimsi. Tam reikia kurti palanki investicin aplink ir veikime kryptingai  derindami veiksmus tarp institucij ir matydami bendr tiksl. Kaip k padarysime? Tikiuosi, iandienos susitikime pavyks pasidalyti, ne tik pastebjimais, valgomis ir priekaitais, bet ir konstruktyviais pasilymais, kuriuos gyvendin tursime geresnes finansines paslaugas visiems visoje alyje. Title: High-Level Fintech Forum Welcome Speech
text: 03/08/22, 14:30 ffl'I:) LI.ET UVQS B,AN KAS 171 High-Level Fintech Forum Welcome Speech I Bank of Lithuania 171 High-LeveFl intechForumWelcomeSpeech 2019-11-27 WelcomespeechbyVitasVasiliauskasC, hairmanof the Boardof the Bankof Lithuania,at the 171 HighLevelFintechForum. Dear Deputy Governor Zhu Hexin, Governors, Ministers, Distinguished Guests, Welcome to the very first 17 1 High-Level Fintech Forum . This Forum marks the beginning of a new chapter for the 17 1 format. We are officially opening a new track for cooperation between China and Central and Eastern Europe - a track on fintech. a, of 1 As part of this dedicated forum, we will also establish the Digital 171 Fintech Coordination Centre. This Centre will provide a platform for the participating countries to have continuous dialogue in the area of financial technologies, thus making full use of our partnership potential. I am honoured that all of this is happening here, in Vilnius - an emerging cluster of financial innovation . My short intervention today will focus on three key building blocks. First, the potential contribution of fintech to global economic development and international trade . Second, the importance of not only benefits, but also risk management. And finally, the role of financial technologies in strengthening economic ties between China and our region. Ladies and Gentlemen, Let me begin with the issue of fintech, economic growth and trade - the focus of our first session . Today, the world economy is under stress due to global trade tensions. International trade is stumbling, and supply chains are feeling the squeeze. The IMF now projects a mere 1.1% world trade growth for 2019 . This is a sharp decline from 2017, when trade was growing 5 times faster. 1/3 03/08/22, 14:30 171 High-Level Fintech Forum Welcome Speech I Bank of Lithuania In this context, we need to think outside the box. I believe that fintech can improve the speed and efficiency of the way companies pay international suppliers, fund foreign operations, or repatriate profits - making cross-border business easier. In this regard, we already have good and practical examples to turn to. For some time now, Hong Kong and Singapore have been engaged in a joint innovation project, led by the respective central banks, called the Global Trade Connectivity Network. This project links trade finance platforms of both territories using blockchain technology. Setting up a digital corridor helps to deal with the inefficiency of the paper-based trade finance system. Such solutions can go a long way to facilitate global commerce and bring greater economic prosperity. However, as in this example, they require close international cooperation - something that we are developing in this event. My second point deals with managing the risks of financial technologies - from money-laundering concerns to cyber-security, data protection, and potential financial stability implications. At the Bank of Lithuania, we have worked hard to advance fintech growth - while always keeping a close eye on the potential risks. We had to change our regulatory mindset - today, we are operating not merely as a watchdog, but also as a partner of the financial sector. Such an attitude is necessary for gaining a deeper understanding of innovative business models. You cannot trail behind market developments if you want to address the associated risks in a timely manner. Let me give you some examples of how this works in practice. We are operating a Newcomer Programme an increasingly popular, one-stop-shop for consultations on all issues that prospective market entrants may have. We also run a regulatory sandbox - a controlled regulatory environment for testing innovative financial products before they reach the market. Such interaction with potential or new market participants is, indeed, a two-way street. It not only helps fintechs navigate our regulations - it also allows us to identify risks at an early stage and take action immediately. The Bank of Lithuania pays particular attention to AML risks. For instance, we have substantially boosted human resources devoted to the issue, and enhanced inter-institutional cooperation in this field. Additionally, we have taken a step further by engaging the private sector and building a wide-ranging AML alliance. More specifically, in a joint effort with other public authorities, we have proposed an initiative to establish a national public-private AML competence centre. This centre would provide a platform for strategic and tactical coordination on AML-related issues. 2/3 03/08/22, 14:30 171 High-LevelFintechForumWelcomeSpeech I Bankof Lithuania Given the cross-border nature of fintech, I believe that formats like the 17 1 can play a crucial role in enhancing the existing international cooperation set-up on managing the associated risks. My third and final message concerns economic ties between the 17 1 participants. I mentioned that fintech can help accelerate global commerce. I believe it can also do precisely that for trade between China and Europe, and CEE countries in particular. Let me give you an example how. At the Bank of Lithuania, we operate a payment system called CENTROLink. The system allows one to reach 34 Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA)countries with ease. Crucially, we have opened the system up to fintech entities directly. This, together with other fintech-oriented regulatory steps, has permitted us to position Lithuania as a gateway for third-country fintechs to enter Europe's payments and banking markets. Several fintechs from China have already used this gateway, and more have expressed interest in doing so. New fintech entities with an EU licence can help eliminate existing bottlenecks in the financial sector infrastructure - for instance, by making cross-border retail payments between the EU and China faster, cheaper, and more efficient. This will make it easier for businesses across Europe to reach the booming Chinese consumer class - and, indeed, for Chinese firms to trade more in Europe. Dear colleagues, We have all the necessary elements for fruitful cooperation on fintech. The 17 1 framework, which constitutes a platform for building trust across borders. Policy-makers keen to advance the fintech agenda forward. Countries full of opportunity and unlocked potential. And - a vibrant host-country to serve as a launching pad for new projects and ideas. Thank you. SuP-ervisionof financial market P-articiP-antsF. intech 3/3

Title: Speech at the scientific conference "Adapting to uncertainties in a changing world"
text: 03/08/22, 14:31 V. Vasiliausko kalba mokslineje konferencijoje . Dearguests,researchers,and members of the central banking community, Welcometo our virtual event hosted by the Bankof Lithuaniaand dedicatedto uncertainty. As the famous saying goes, nothing is certain except Q 1 is1 for death and taxes. And yet,we do not reallyknow who was the first speakthese words. Somesources mention BenjaminFranklin,others say Mark Twain. As you can see, we cannot evenbe certain about this statement on certainty. Therefore,I think we can paraphrase: nothing is certain exceptfor uncertainty. The pandemic has surely demonstratedthis. Indeed,noneof the earlywarning systems had predictedthe global outbreak of the virus. Another keytakeawayfrom this crisis experienceis that uncertainty and globalizationgo hand-in-hand. Globalizationmakes it easierfor tail eventsto ripplethroughout the planet - and producetruly global shocks. In the euro area,uncertainty has substantially increasedsince 2010.Takea look at the graph,which displays both the indexfor EconomicPolicy Uncertaintyand the World UncertaintyIndex. The sovereigndebt crisis, Brexit,trade tensions,and,most recently, the pandemic - all of these factors, contributing to uncertainty, havebeenshapedand reinforcedby globalization. ... 1/3 03/08/22, 14:31 V. Vasiliauskokalbamokslinejekonferencijoje.Prisitaikymasprieneapibreztum4kintanciamepasaulyje"(angl4kalba) I Lietuvosba... Today's event itself is a good example of globalization in action: cooperating with our colleagues from the National Bank of Poland, Centre for Economic Policy Research, and the Central Bank Research Association, we have gathered together scholars from different parts of the planet to discuss uncertainty in a globalized world. The timing of the conference is also, I believe, very appropriate. There is uncertainty surrounding almost every aspect of the COVID-19 crisis. In such times, firms pause investment and hiring, and the risk of resource misallocation increases. Consumers tend to save more for precautionary reasons. This behavior can produce long-term scarring effects that are difficult to predict. For policy makers, such extreme uncertainty poses a substantial challenge. Indeed, it forces them to reconsider some of their core assumptions. This is not necessarily a bad thing. Uncertainty can be a catalyst for change. For instance, the COVID-19 shock has caused a shift in mindset in terms of the policy response that is possible on a European level. The EU's recovery fund will set a precedent for economic integration and risksharing in Europe that seemed almost inconceivable prior to the pandemic. Systemic central banks have acted rapidly and forcefully as well. We at the Governing Council of the ECB have launched the special Pandemic Emergency Purchase Programme, which features some novel and bold modalities safeguarding medium-term price and financial stability. The ECB has also fine-tuned its forward guidance to help markets and the broader society navigate today's uncertain waters. But central banks can arguably still do more - and we will discuss this in our first session today. In addition, speakers will shed a much-needed light on trading firms' behavior, as well as trade- and macrorelated effects of uncertainty. Lithuanian data is used in one of the contributions, helping us learn how firms adjust when trade abruptly stops. This is a key topic for open economies like Lithuania. Unfortunately, this conference has also been marked by a profoundly heart-breaking and unexpected event. Two months ago the profession of economics suddenly lost one of its brightest minds - Emmanuel Farhi, who was supposed to give a keynote speech here in this conference. Emmanuel covered a wide range of research areas - and displayed a clear motivation to help policy makers make better decisions. We will all miss him dearly. I hope that this conference can build on and celebrate Emmanuel's legacy. . 03/08/22, 14:31 V. Vasiliauskokalbamokslinejekonferencijoje.Prisitaikymasprieneapibreztum4kintanciamepasaulyje"(angl4kalba) I Lietuvosba... In this vein, I expect that our knowledge-sharing will help policy makers deal with uncertainty. We are thus happy to have three distinguished keynote speakers with us, namely Professors Beata Javorcik, Jennifer L'.ao and Kalina Manova. They will shed fresh light on the role of informational frictions in business cycle fluctuations, gains from globalization in the presence potential resource misallocation, and local labour market effects of the Brexit vote. I would like to thank Andrei and Julian from CEBRA,as well as Phillippe from CEPRfor their invaluable help in organizing this conference. I also sincerely thank colleagues from the National Bank of Poland: Governor Glapinski, who will deliver welcome remarks as well; and the bank's Research and International Relations departments. And last but not least, many thanks to the team at the Bank of Lithuania for bringing the idea of this conference all the way to fruition. To wrap up, I am very happy to see this conference remaining a tradition despite the difficult circumstances - thus adding a degree of certainty to our uncertain times. Thank you. I wish you fruitful and enlightening discussions.

Title: AML pendulum: towards equilibrium
text: 03/08/22 , 14:30 ffl'I:) LI.ETUVQS B,AN KAS Speech by J. Gavina I Bank of Lithuania "AMLpendulum:towardsequilibrium"s,peechby JekaterinaGavina 2021-03-31 JekaterinaGovina,Directorof the FinancialMarket SupervisionService,took part in ACAMSAntiFinancialCrimeVirtualSymposiumBalticson 31 March2021. Shedeliveredthe keynotespeech"AML pendulum:towardsequilibrium". Good morning everyone . It is a great pleasure to share with you my thoughts and at the same time it is a great pity I can do it only virtually . a, of 1 My keynote is about the reality that we were (and still are) observing in the region for the last 3-5 years and what we should do about that. By the way, this is how a pendulum looks like. For me, it symbolises the swinging in the financial market's approach towards AML from one side (more liberal and flexible approach) to the other (conservative), until it reaches the state of equilibrium. So that is the past and some headlines from the most significant recent cases where Scandinavian banks were sanctioned or are being investigated because of loose AML controls that caused (mainly) reputational damage to the region . And we feel the consequences of that right now . So, besides the struggle of financial companies and specifically banks themselves to obtain and maintain correspondent banking relationships, the consequences are that some of the categories of clients, like NGOs, companies trading with counterparties from third countries, even ordinary people, face difficulties dealing with banks . And although in most cases it seems to be justifiable, there are some cases where the pendulum is far from the equilibrium. And it is not only the case in the Nordic-Baltic region , but rather a much wider issue . Even the European Banking Authority and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) recognise that the issue is worth examining further. The FATFjust recently announced that it is going to launch the initiative "mitigating the unintended 1/2 03/08/22, 14:30 Speech by J. Gavina I Bank of Lithuania consequences of the FATFstandards", analysing the issue of de risking, financial exclusion, etc. Here in Lithuania, we are investigating the de risking phenomenon as well - to understand the reasons and the affected part of the society. We are going to share our findings by the end of this year. Let's move to the desirable equilibrium of the state of affairs. I do not believe in a world with no criminals and no money laundering or terrorist financing. There was such, but it was a long time ago - before Adam bit the forbidden fruit. And as we have been exiled from paradise from that moment, we must accept the world as it is. With its good and evil. Nevertheless, I believe in a world that maximises its efforts and potential to be the best possible one. And in the AML area, the gravitational force that should attract the pendulum to the state of equilibrium is the demands of our society. And the demands are obvious- to have access to a payment account, to trade freely and so on. And thinking about the restoring force of the pendulum, I think more and more people come to the conclusion that it should be the partnerships: greater collaboration within the private sector (among banks, between banks and flntech companies), between the private sector and the public sector, and between public sector authorities both on a national and a supranational level. And here I would like to take the chance and announce about the project that I personally and my team were working very hard on and are especially proud of - the Centre of Excellence in AML. I am very proud to announce that we have just reached the final stage to establish the next level partnership: approved the Centre's CEO,so the Centre will start operations in the coming months. Thank you for your attention. I wish you an interesting conference and a promising partnership. To maximise our efforts to achieve equilibrium. Title: Interview to BNS news agency
text: Interview of V. Vasiliauskas to BNS news agency Vitas Vasiliauskas, Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania, is interviewed by BNS journalist sarunas Sabaitis.  A decade ago, you took charge of the Bank of Lithuania after the end of the financial crisis, now you are leaving the Central Bank before the end of the new crisis. Has much changed in that decade?  I will start with the fact that the crisis of the last decade was different  it was a real economic financial crisis, and the current crisis is, above all, pandemic, and therefore the difference is huge. More than a decade ago, we entered the crisis completely unprepared, naively hoping that we would avoid it, that it would pass by the side. At the moment, the situation is different, the economy has been much stronger, and if you look back at 2020, it is clear that the consequences of the crisis are also different. I believe that a lot of components have contributed to this, and of these, membership of the euro area is in the unsung place, which has led to the fact that we have been able to afford large injections of public finances into the economy. When we see less than one per cent of the economy that contracted last year and the number of deficits that increased, it means that large sums of money have certainly been poured in. This is obvious proof that this time everything is different.  A decade ago, one of the features of the crisis was the lack of credit, now it seems that there is really no shortage of money. "Indeed, in the previous crisis, liquidity problems quickly became solvency problems, and there is no liquidity problem in this crisis. Of course, the sectors most affected have been hit hard and they will need more time to recover, of course, if we return to that normal environment. However, finance is certainly not a problem, and we are now seeing a coordinated jump between central banks and governments, which was indeed lacking in the previous crisis. As far as Lithuania's economic structure is concerned, I would also think that we were much more prepared. What we noticed during 2020, in the export markets we managed to grow our muscles even more, to improve our situation.  That question of excess money will have to be resolved somehow sooner or later?  Of course, it will have to be resolved, but I do not think that this is a problem, because the economic contractions in the larger Member States of the European Union have been really impressive, and the coordination of fiscal and monetary policy will have to continue in the future. I really don't believe how armageddonic scenarios are sometimes heard that inflation is about to jump terribly upwards. The euro system does not predict high inflation, but should, in principle, be as it is now, with some jumps in the course of this year, but it is still a long way from achieving the 2% medium-term objective.  There has been talk that the European Central Bank can also revise the 2% inflation target itself.  A strategic discussion is ongoing and its results are expected to be reflected in the communication of the European Central Bank in September. I don't think it's close to the two percent inflationary target  As far as coordinated solutions are concerned, can we also expect some kind of joint solution to reduce the level of public debt that has increased during the crisis? "I think coordination is plausible because the crisis of 2008 and the current crisis have shown that coordination is better than acting alone. But the main recipe for reducing debt is, in fact, economic development. There is no other recipe. Therefore, it is very important that the extra money that comes in is used purposefully.  Is it safe to say that managing the current crisis will become a benchmark for how future crises will be dealt with? "I hope that there will only be more common solutions and that the degree of economic convergence and federalism in the European Union will only deepen. I believe that in future we will also be able to talk about common debt instruments, both within the euro area and throughout the European Union. The more we integrate, the safer and stronger we should feel in every sense, and the more opportunities there will be for the development of our economy. The more we integrate, the safer and stronger we should feel in every sense, and the more opportunities there will be for the development of our economy.  We heard talk of common borrowing instruments as early as last year, but they did not materialise. This was due to a lack of willpower or lack of need?  I think everything has been overshadowed by the pandemic situation. Still, those waves, now apparently, the hot issue is the pace of vaccination. But sooner or later, there will certainly be a return to this issue, although, of course, when the situation returns to normal, some pressure may be lost, which I believe is healthy for the European Union. But again, economic thought is advanced and I see no other reason than to move on to the development of co-borrower instruments.  Do you not think that greater federalism in the European Union will reduce the autonomy of individual states and their influence? "I don't really see the danger of that. When I talk about federalism and nation-states, I always give the example of the United States, which, starting with the confederation, later became a federation. I am talking, in particular, about economic matters, about the financial market, because, in my opinion, Europe is not making the most of the opportunities offered by the single market. Also in relations with third parties. All cultural matters are a matter for national politicians, their nurturing and promotion should not be abandoned. But being in the European Union is, geopolitically, the only way for us to survive. - Still, the story is ruthless. Large political formations, most often empires, to which some historians also attribute the United States, sooner or later are doomed to failure. "I wouldn't really call the European Union an empire, if we want to use the term already, it has to be stressed that it is built on a sufficiently democratic basis. Of course, one must always keep one's own interests in mind and defend them, but a small state needs to do so through the formation of alliances and alliances. For speaking not in a straight light, but for pronunciation in various formats. It's not like that  As far as the European institutions are concerned, the European Central Bank was probably also much better prepared for this crisis than it was a decade ago?  Without a doubt, for example, a decade ago, talking about asset acquisition programs was an unimaginable thing at all. I believe that the European Central Bank is one of the most European institutions and has indeed demonstrated flexibility and the ability to coordinate with fiscal policy during the pandemic. That one's gratifying, it's a new reality. Despite the differences in the architecture of the European Union from, for example, the USA, where the mandate of the Federal Reserve System is the labor market and price stability. Our mandate is only price stability. From this formal point of view alone, those differences are there, but in my opinion, the last reaction shows very clearly that the euro system can be flexible. Of course, there will still be quite a few questions in the future, and let us remember the constitutional issues of some of the States of the Community, but Europe is moving forward.  Can it be predicted that the tough stance on the level of public debt or fiscal deficits that has prevailed in Europe so far may be mitigated?  Let's distinguish between two things, borrowing when needed and the purposeful use and spending of borrowed money. These are two different things, and I am certainly not giving up the idea that Member States need to act responsibly and, above all, use that borrowed money to ease economic constraints, but on the other hand, the money must also be used for the structural reforms that you have to do to increase your competitiveness in the future. As for Lithuania, every year we receive recipes from various international organizations, for example, the International Monetary Fund, the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development. Education, health care, social exclusion, the labour market are those areas that relate both to human capital and to infrastructure. They need to be invested in. I believe that the current crisis, especially the recovery measures that are being put in place now, will be structured so that we can move forward. We have many long-standing problems and their solution is mandatory as a homework preparation for the student. If you prepare them, you can expect a positive assessment, if you do not prepare, you will sit in your tail again. We have many long-standing problems and their solution is mandatory as a homework preparation for the student.  For me, Lithuania is more like not an advanced student, but an average learner, who does only that part of his homework to report to the teacher, but does not try to go further himself.  I think our troubles are also related to the fact that there is no discipline in the classroom. Those who sit in a galloque and later have the opportunity to come to the first bench often forget what problems they had when sitting in the back of the classroom. Therefore, there is that constant exchange of places, instead of doing a class meeting and agreeing that we will learn one thing or another for the next ten years.  Can we expect that consensus to be reached sooner or later? "I'm an optimist, so I think there's going to be more and more civil maturity and agreement, not controversy until the last feather.  Another distinctive feature of the current crisis is the rising capital markets, real estate prices. This shows that some of the money to stimulate the economy is deposited in the pockets of a higher-class society. Do you not think that this will further increase social segregation and exclusion?  If we speak globally, then apparently it is. If we are talking about Lithuania, then our economic structure is interesting in that during the crisis, income inequality and exclusion are precisely reduced. We noticed this after the crisis of 2008, and I think it is happening now. Then, when the development begins, that separation of curves happens again. But the issues of income, inequality of property status do not go anywhere from the agenda. I think these are things of political economy and they will certainly be relevant. But again, there are other means for this, these are already issues of national social policy. Because monetary policy, no matter how large the euro system may be, is, in principle, primarily concerned with the economy and probably cannot deal with social affairs.  Would the common level of the European Union's minimum wage, the common taxes, help to solve these problems? The debate on this issue is ongoing.  Yes, I would think that this is also the agenda for those issues that need to be dealt with jointly. But again, here, first of all, it will depend on the joint agreements between the Member States. Because even now we hear a lot of different opinions. How much of that sovereignty of states can be transferred to a pan-European level will also determine the success of the debate.  Let's go back maybe then to our banking system. What did you find her and what do you leave behind?  I leave it perhaps more focused, because the two largest banks and one large branch really occupy 80% of the total market in terms of assets. In 2011, there were definitely more of those players. But, in my opinion, there is currently no threat to financial stability, the system is much stronger than it was in 2011. Corporate culture, I think, is completely different. Well, in 2011, we did what any sensible caretaker would have done  we dealt with problems that were piling up.  Is it safe to say that during your tenure you have cleared the banking system from unreliable players?  I think so.  The Bank of Lithuania was very active in trying to attract Chinese investments to the banking sector, and there was even talk of the arrival of one traditional Chinese bank. However, due to geopolitical processes, these plans had to be abandoned.  You see, it all depends on the position of the state, because we are not acting in isolation. We are part of a greenhouse named Lithuania. And if the state's position has changed, then naturally we adapt too. That's what we needed clarity all the time, in that sense. And now that clarity is there. We have an investment portfolio, we were among the first in the euro system to invest in China. We in the euro system, along with several other central banks, are also known as having know-how to invest. But apparently those hopes that the retail bank would come did not come true. And in general, no fundamentally new bigger player has come. New players such as specialized  What is the European Central Bank's approach to Chinese investment?  It is indifferent, in other words, neutral. It's just that the position is such that you can't ignore it, because the yuan is the reserve currency included in the IMF basket, well, and that's all that's said. China is the second largest economy, so it cannot ignore that fact. Political debate is not a factor to which a technocratic institution such as the euro system, the European Central Bank or any central bank can react or play some kind of active role.  Is there a chance that the value of the yuan as a reserve currency will increase?  I would think that this is directly related to China's economic growth, so I would say that it is.  Could this jeopardise the status of the euro as a reserve currency?  History shows that global reserve currencies can very quickly change their role. I can give an example of a pound sterling compared to the US dollar. At the beginning of the twentieth century, the ratios of these currencies were completely different than at the end of the century or in the twenty-first century. I believe that the steps on the so-called e-euro are the right ones, but a little overdue. We can state the fact that, in the area of e-currency or e-money, China is at an advanced stage and is already using this in individual provinces. To the extent that Europe will be able to make a breakthrough in the area of the e-currency, I believe that it will also contribute to the strength of the euro as a currency. So far, I do not see the significance of the euro in cross-border settlements at stake.  The example of the British pound sterling and the US dollar clearly shows that the meaning of the currency is inseparable from the economic and political power of its state. The European Union's efforts to regain production capacity and to invest in research must also strengthen the euro's position. "I think it's directly related. Without a doubt, the size and power of the economy and inseparable from the influence of the state and the significance of its monetary unit in the international space. In my opinion, we are currently facing several processes taking place at the same time the high rate of globalisation, which has, admittedly, stalled recently, and national interests. In my opinion, however, Europe can only be strong if it is united, and the times of the strong Member States are already in the past. One Germany, one France, one Spain as individual players have much less potential of international significance than the European Union as a unified economic area. In my opinion, everyone, both the old and the new Member States, have won from the European Union project.  Can you share your plans for the future? What are you going to do until the beginning of 2023, when you start working on the Board of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), where you will represent the Nordic-Baltic region?  I don't have any plans yet. I have a few private offers, but there is a general cooling-off period for the system, so I would have to obtain the consent of the Ethics Committee of the European Central Bank for a certain period of time in order to get a job. As a rule, at least half a year, and the cooling period lasts from one to two years, this consent cannot be expected. I think in the near future just  But you probably won't abandon the financial field?  It's very important to ensure, as I say, that burning by 2023. In the International Monetary Fund, with the change of US administration, very interesting things are now happening, and from the closure and the IMF's agenda of reducing the significance of the IMF, it is returning with a completely opposite approach.  Do you think that, in the aftermath of this crisis, both the IMF and other international organisations will play a stronger role in the global economic and political sphere? "I'm really hoping and I'd really wish it. The recent crisis showed that the algorithm of systematic and co-made decisions works much better than when digging out of problems on its own.  And to conclude, what would you like to wish the future Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Lithuania?  I would just wish for teamwork, the realization that leading the central bank is the pinnacle of a career and everything that comes after that will be just walking downhill. Therefore, I would like to wish you to stand high first, look behind the horizon, fight by all means for the independence of the Bank of Lithuania and withdraw with dignity after the completion of the works. "Thank you for the conversation."
